Name: 100Unicorns
Description: 100Unicorns is an accelerator and venture capital fund manager based in Andheri East, Mumbai. It was previously called 9Unicorns, and it sits within the Venture Catalysts group: the copyright line on every page of its site names Venture Catalyst Accelerator LLP, and its Corporate Day event was run with Venture Catalysts and their group company Incubate Hub. It backs startups from idea stage to angel stage, and describes itself as an accelerator programme backed by founders and CXOs rather than as an incubator with a campus. It is a fund first. Support comes with investment, so joining means taking money for equity. 100Unicorns runs two funds registered with SEBI as Alternative Investment Funds. Fund I is registered as the 9Unicorns Accelerator Fund, a Category I venture capital fund, managed by Venture Catalysts Accelerator LLP. Fund II is registered as 100Unicorns, a Category II fund, managed by 9Unicorns Accelerator Private Limited. Both registration numbers are published on the site's regulatory page. How to apply to 100Unicorns There is one way in. The Apply Now button on the home page and the portfolio page opens an online application titled "100Unicorns - Startup Application". It is open all year. No cohort number, intake window or closing date appears anywhere on the site, so there is nothing to wait for. After you submit, the confirmation says the team will come back to you in seven to fourteen days. The application asks for the startup's name and website, what it does in fifty characters, the problem and who faces it, and what you are building. It then asks about the founding team: how many founders there are, their names and email addresses, their backgrounds, and how long they have known each other. The idea section asks why you picked this problem, what is new about your approach, what people use instead today, who your competitors in India are, how you will make money, and how you will get users. The progress section asks whether people are already using the product, how many customers you have, and your revenue for the last full calendar year. You also submit a link to your deck on Drive or Dropbox, say what support you need beyond capital, and note any incubator or accelerator you have already joined. Who can apply Early-stage startups, from idea stage through angel stage. The site says the investment focus is broad and spans many sectors, with preferences shifting with market trends. Its portfolio pages group companies under SaaS and deep tech, fintech, edtech, B2B tech, consumer and D2C, healthtech, mobility, media and entertainment, agritech, sportstech, defence and advanced manufacturing. The application form asks for your location as city and country rather than restricting applicants to India. What you get beyond capital 100Unicorns lists six things it adds to its cheque: mentorship from experienced startup founders, sector scouts and industry veterans; strategic guidance and network access through people it calls Sector Anchors; a place at its D Day global demo day; growth capital connections through an event it calls Prostar; a network of global investors, founders and CXOs; and corporate governance coaching. D Day is its demo day for portfolio companies, run online for an investor network the site describes as more than 1,500 global venture capital funds and family offices. Four editions have been held. The most recent one named on the site, DDay 4, ran on 18 October 2023 with 15 startups across agritech, consumer brands, deeptech, e-commerce, edtech, financial services, fintech, HR tech and media. Selection is described as deliberate, favouring startups with a track record and a focus on profitability and growth. C Day, or Corporate Day, is a sector-themed event that introduces portfolio startups to corporate buyers. The site calls it quarterly. Its first edition covered consumer packaged goods and retail, drew more than 70 corporates and over 35 senior corporate representatives, and showcased nine startups. The governance work is a workshop run with the law firm Nishith Desai & Associates at the firm's LP Day in 2025, where founders signed a Statement of Commitment to Good Governance. None of these three is something you apply to. They are run for companies already in the portfolio, so the open application is the only door. Scale The numbers on the site do not all agree, so treat them as its own claims. The home page counters say more than 14,000 startups reviewed and 157 investments, with 45 soonicorns and three unicorns among them. The portfolio page says Fund I backed more than 150 startups between 2020 and 2025, while the founders page says more than 500 founders have been backed globally. The portfolio grid itself lists about 150 Fund I companies and three featured Fund II companies: 1BUY.AI, Rotoris and HiFy. On its own impact numbers, portfolio companies have created more than 25,000 direct jobs, 21 percent of the portfolio is led by women founders, and companies from more than 27 tier II and tier III cities have been backed. Who runs it The team page names four co-founders: Dr. Apoorva Ranjan Sharma, who is also Co-Founder and Managing Partner, Anil Jain, Anuj Golecha and Gaurav Jain. Rishabh Golchha is a Partner and Vinod Keni is CFO, with principals, associates and an analyst alongside them, plus a compliance and legal team. A separate investment committee and a set of global partners covering MENA, South East Asia and Africa are also listed. There is no careers page; hiring enquiries go to a team inbox. Where it is 100Unicorns works from B 901, Times Square, near Marol Metro Station, Andheri East, Mumbai 400059. No other office is listed, and the site does not mention any co-working space, lab or incubation centre of its own.

Description: 36Inc, which operates under the name AIC@36Inc, is a business incubator and accelerator based in Raipur, Chhattisgarh. It describes itself as the first business incubator cum accelerator supported by the Government of Chhattisgarh, and it works with both new startups and existing companies that want to grow. It runs from City Centre Mall in central Raipur. What they support 36Inc works across sectors rather than specialising in one. It helps founders take an idea towards a working business, and it also supports existing companies looking to scale. The support it describes includes mentorship, management guidance, funding support, co-working space and technological assistance. The teams it has backed have worked in areas such as health technology, drones and 3D printing. Programmes The core offer is open incubation, run from the 36Inc space in Raipur. Founders apply through the Apply for Incubation route on the organisation's site, or by writing to its office. 36Inc also hosts a MeitY TIDE 2.0 programme, the central government's Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs scheme, which founders apply to through the dedicated page on its site. Track record 36Inc has run cohorts under the Startup Chhattisgarh banner. Its first batch brought together 30 startups working in fields such as health technology, drones and 3D printing. The organisation's own pages are the source for these figures. How to apply Applications for incubation are made through the Apply for Incubation link on the 36Inc site, or by contacting the office directly. The published intake dates and eligibility details are not stated clearly on the pages that could be read, so founders should check the current status on the site or ask the team before applying.

Name: 888VC
Description: 888VC (also written 888vc) is a venture firm based in Whitefield, Bengaluru. Its website describes a cross-border model that links Indian startups with investors in India, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. It runs the GRO8 accelerator for founders, an invite-only investor community called GRO8 Club, and invests in early-stage companies. The site names Network888 Accelerator LLP as the operating entity. The GRO8 accelerator The accelerator is 888VC's route for founders who want to raise from outside India. It is a 12-week programme, presented as a journey from MVP to market-ready, and it ends with a Demo Day. The site describes four phases: strategy and validation in weeks one to three, product and sales in weeks four to six, finance and operations in weeks seven to nine, and fundraising and Demo Day in weeks ten to twelve. Along the way founders get one-to-one sessions with experienced founders and senior operators, plus curated introductions to investors in India, the US and the UAE. The site also lists workspace, legal support, accounting and vendor credits under ecosystem access. The site does not publish intake dates, a deadline, a fee policy or any equity or investment terms for the accelerator. Its application button reads Apply for Next Cohort, and it leads to an online application form. Who can apply The site sets four criteria. First, early traction: pre-seed or seed-stage with early market validation, a product in market and a clear go-to-market plan. Second, global ambition: you think beyond India from day one, and cross-border scale is part of your plan. Third, a technology-driven business. Fourth, a long-term mindset. The sectors listed are deep tech, AI and machine learning, consumer, healthtech, sustainability, manufacturing, fintech and SaaS or B2B. Investing and the GRO8 Club 888VC also invests directly. Its site says it backs companies from seed to Series A and that it stays involved through pivots and later fundraises. Press reports in September 2025 said 888VC had launched a maiden fund, registered with SEBI as a Category I alternative investment fund in February 2025, to back early-stage deep tech startups. The site does not state this registration, and it does not say how the fund relates to the accelerator. The site and the press also give different cheque sizes, and the site does not say whether they describe the same vehicle. GRO8 Club is for investors, not founders. It is an invite-only community of angels, family offices, funds and senior operators who receive curated pitch decks and due-diligence summaries and can invest through syndicate vehicles, including a dollar-based feeder structure for cross-border deals. Founders do not apply to it for funding. Track record These are 888VC's own claims and its sources do not agree. The site says it has invested in more than 50 startups, while reports from September 2025 quoted the firm saying it had funded over 20 companies. The site and the press also give different figures for the combined value of the portfolio. The site says 200 or more investors attended its 2024 Demo Day, and that its network includes more than 200 VC fund partners and more than 1,000 angels, CFOs and CXOs. The portfolio page names Babai Tiffins, DaanVeda, Datazip, Drivers4me, EcoRatings, GetCrest.ai, HomeCapital, IGoWise, Multipl, Pick My Work, Sanfe and UKHI. These are companies 888VC invested in, not necessarily accelerator participants. The site also says one portfolio company, Finly, was acquired by a US fintech company. Who runs it Rohit Bafna is the founder and CEO. His profile on the site says he has more than ten years of venture experience, and press reports say he previously worked at 100Unicorns. The site gives no founding year, and one press report says the firm was founded in 2022. Contact and location The site gives its address as Whitefield, Bengaluru 560066, and info@888vc.co as the contact email. The accelerator is offered in India, the United States and the United Arab Emirates.

Name: ACSEL Technology Forum
Description: ACSEL Technology Forum is an AI organisation in Bengaluru, set up as a Section 8 company under the aegis of the IIT Alumni Centre, Bengaluru (IITACB) and supported by the Government of Karnataka. It runs the Avinya accelerator for early-stage AI startups, alongside research, conferences and community work on responsible AI. It sits on the second floor of the IIT Alumni Centre Bengaluru campus in Bommasandra Industrial Area. ACSEL describes itself as a hub for responsible AI innovation, working across startups, research and collaboration between industry, academia and government. In its own press material it calls itself an AI Centre of Excellence under IITACB. Artificial intelligence is the only field it works in, and the human-centric, responsible side of AI is the thread running through all of its work. How programmes work The one programme a founder can apply to is Avinya, ACSEL's accelerator. The name comes from the Sanskrit word for innovation. It is a structured programme of sixteen weeks, described elsewhere on the site as four months, and it takes ten startups per batch. Avinya is built in two phases. In the first, every startup in the cohort receives seed investment. In the second, ACSEL makes personalised introductions to investors matched to the startup's stage and industry, and can invest further in the best performers from the cohort. The programme ends in a Demo Day where startups pitch to a curated audience of investors and partners. ACSEL's rules describe the initial money as a grant or an equity-linked instrument, released against milestones and subject to due diligence and progress reports. The teaching side runs on mentorship pods, where each startup gets dedicated mentors drawn from IIT alumni, entrepreneurs, domain experts and strategists. There are regular one-on-one strategy sessions to track progress, peer circles across the cohort, and expert workshops on fundraising, scaling and product development. Startups pick their own industry learning track, with pathways in FinTech, HealthTech and Climate Tech. A resource toolkit covers legal, financial and marketing support. ACSEL also gives cohort startups curated datasets to work with, and says it runs global exchange opportunities through partnerships with international accelerators. Founders who finish join the ACSEL Alumni Network, which gets access to events, investors and resources. Alumni are expected to mentor later cohorts. Applications for Cohort 3 opened on 7 September 2026 and close on 10 October 2026, with orientation of the cohort on 3 November 2026 and Demo Day in February 2027. Twenty applicants will be shortlisted from the forms. Outside the accelerator, ACSEL runs events and publishing rather than programmes. Its first International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, "Reimagining AI", ran over two days on 22 and 23 January 2026 at the IIT Alumni Centre, with tracks on healthcare AI, responsible AI, climate AI and the road ahead. Name: APIARY - A Centre of Entrepreneurship in Blockchain Technology
Description: APIARY is the Centre of Entrepreneurship in Blockchain Technology, run by the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) at its incubation facility in Gurugram, Haryana. It was set up with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Government of Haryana and industry and academic partners, to find and support early-stage blockchain start-ups. The centre began with a soft launch of its Idea Challenge Programme in 2020. How the programmes work Start-ups enter through the Idea Challenge Programme, an open call for Indian start-ups working in blockchain. Selected start-ups move into a three-month incubation at the Gurugram centre, which can be extended to six months. During incubation they validate the idea through industry contact, build a proof of concept or MVP, acquire their first customers, set up a revenue stream and payment cycle, and write a business plan. Start-ups that complete these tasks become eligible for a nine-month acceleration programme, with unlimited mentorship and masterclasses on going to market, data and business models, and pitching to investors. The site also runs a pre-incubation opportunity for engineering students in their second, third and fourth years, who can be incubated as blockchain start-ups. The site lists past editions of the Idea Challenge Programme, numbered 2.0 to 5.0. It does not show dates for the current intake, so check the Apply Now link before planning around a deadline. Who can apply The Idea Challenge Programme is for Indian start-ups working in a blockchain domain. Start-ups registered with DPIIT under Startup India are encouraged to apply. An applicant must have been registered or incorporated within the last 10 years when the challenge opens, must have an annual turnover within the programme's limit for the financial years since incorporation, and must be innovative and scalable. Individual academicians, researchers, educators, entrepreneurs, partnership firms and LLPs may also apply. If selected, they must register as a private limited company, preferably within three months. The pre-incubation opportunity is for engineering students in their second to fourth year. Facilities The centre is hosted in the STPI Gurugram incubation facility. The site lists ready-to-work plug-and-play space, high-speed internet, a network operations centre, a workspace that runs around the clock, round-the-clock security and a support team. It states a dedicated 80-seat co-working space and a dedicated blockchain platform. Start-ups developing blockchain platforms and products are offered co-working space during pre-incubation, allocated under STPI policy. Mentoring and support Mentors help start-ups validate their ideas, build the product and reach the market. They also connect start-ups with prototyping and manufacturing vendors, and the centre offers mentor access through an online portal. Need-based sessions cover legal, compliance, branding and cyber security. STPI has an arrangement with the National Research and Development Corporation (NRDC) for patent drafting and filing, trademarks and copyright. Marketing support includes an end-to-end marketing plan, knowledge sessions, road shows and networking events. Who runs it STPI is an autonomous society set up by MeitY in 1991 to promote software exports. The centre has a governing council, and STPI's Director General chairs it. STPI Next, a Section 8 company incorporated by STPI, acts as the nodal agency for its start-up activities. The Government of Haryana provides financial aid to the centre. Scale so far The homepage shows a self-reported dashboard of five cohort rows. The first cohort lists 413 registered applicants, 85 applications received, 47 shortlisted, 18 screened in and 14 mentors. The rows are undated, and two of them are labelled cohort 4, so the figures do not line up cleanly across cohorts. The site does not state how many start-ups have graduated. Location The centre is at 6th Floor, C/o STPI, Plot no. 30, Electronic City, Phase IV, Udyog Vihar, Sector 18, Gurugram, Haryana 122015.

Name: Accenture
Description: Accenture is a global professional-services and technology company. This page covers only the one part of it a founder can apply to in India: the Accenture Ventures Tech Next Challenge, an open-innovation competition run once a year from its own site. Nothing here describes the consulting business, and none of Accenture's corporate scale should be read as a track record for the challenge. The challenge is not an incubator. It has no premises of its own, no residency and no rolling intake. It runs as a single annual cycle: applications open, two rounds of evaluation, a shortlist, then a Grand Finale pitch day. The 2026 edition was the eighth, themed around enterprise reinvention through autonomous technologies. It opened on 22 June 2026, closed on 20 July 2026 after a deadline extension, announced its shortlist on 3 August and held the finale on 12 August at the Accenture Innovation Hub in Bangalore. No date has been announced for a ninth edition, so a founder reading this today is between intakes. How the challenge works Applications are made on a single form linked from the challenge site, and you pick one track. There are seven, and each one is tied to an Accenture business unit — what the company calls a Reinvention Partner — that takes solutions to its enterprise clients: Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent. That mapping is the point of the format. Accenture says every finalist gets a direct path to the unit best placed to put their product in front of clients, so the track you choose decides who inside Accenture ends up reading your application. Entries go through two rounds judged by senior Accenture leaders and subject-matter experts from the Reinvention Partners. Shortlisted finalists pitch at the Grand Finale to a jury of CXOs, technology leaders and investors, and one winner is picked in each of the seven tracks. The whole cycle takes about two months. Who can apply The eligibility bar is narrow and the site states it as five conditions you must meet in full. You must be an early or growth-stage startup building defensible, technology-led innovation. You must solve enterprise-grade problems — consumer and prosumer products are excluded by name. Your work must sit in autonomous technologies: autonomous AI and agents, autonomous physical systems, autonomous infrastructure or autonomous operations. You must have an India connection, which can be an India headquarters, an Indian co-founder, or established India operations or engineering. And you must already have delivered paid engagements — pilots or deployments — to enterprise customers. That last condition is the one that rules most applicants out. Accenture says plainly that this is not a seed-stage or ideation programme, and the challenge is aimed at companies past validation that are ready for global enterprise deployments. There is no incorporation-type or state restriction beyond the India-presence test, no fee, and no equity commitment attached to applying. What winners and finalists get Winners are fast-tracked into Accenture and aligned to the Reinvention Partner closest to their product, with go-to-market access to Accenture's global enterprise client base and mentoring from its leadership. That comes with priority consideration for client pilots, named points of contact and solution integration across all seven units. Winners are also put up as candidates for a strategic minority investment from Accenture and given a one-to-one meeting with an investment partner, plus a route into the Accel Atoms programme. The partner benefits sit alongside that: non-dilutive cloud credits from the cloud partner and invitations to its startup events, and inclusion in the NVIDIA Inception programme, which carries developer tools, preferred pricing and exposure to NVIDIA's venture network. Finalists who do not win are not sent away empty-handed. All finalists get priority access to incubation at the Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development at IISc Bangalore, which is where office space and infrastructure come from, subject to availability. Note that the space belongs to FSID, not to Accenture. Scale and recent editions Accenture does not publish cumulative figures for the challenge, so there is no verified total of startups supported. What is on record is per-edition and mostly comes from press coverage. Reports of the 2026 edition put participation at more than 350 startups across the seven tracks. Coverage of the 2025 edition, themed on autonomous AI and judged at the same Bangalore venue, reported over 700 applications, 300 shortlisted and 15 finalists. Accenture's own 2019 announcement, when the programme ran under the Accenture Ventures Challenge name, reported over 370 entries. Treat all of these as reported participation counts for one cycle, not as a measure of startups Accenture has worked with. Locations The challenge has no office you can visit. It is run online up to the finale, and the finale itself is held at the Accenture Innovation Hub in Bangalore, which has also hosted recent editions. Contact details on the challenge site are the personal work addresses of two Accenture staff rather than a programme inbox, so we do not republish them here; use the site's own contact block if you need to reach the team.

Name: Action For India
Description: Action For India (AFI) is an accelerator for tech-enabled social enterprises. It was launched in 2012, is run by its own board of trustees and board of directors, and works from offices in New Delhi and Bangalore, with chapters in Silicon Valley and the UK. Its cohort programmes run online, so a founder can take part from anywhere in India. What AFI does AFI describes itself as a platform to help scale high-potential social entrepreneurs, and defines a social enterprise as any organisation developing products and services that make things better for under-served communities and tries to do it at scale. Its focus areas follow the UN Sustainable Development Goals: education, healthcare, agriculture, energy, livelihoods and financial inclusion. Climate has been added for its 2026-27 cohort. AFI connects founders to capital through its relationships with foundations and funding institutions, to mentors working across industries globally, to technology help from Silicon Valley experts, and to a network of the Indian diaspora. It is worth being clear about what AFI is not. It publishes no labs, no coworking and no incubation space, and its Delhi office is a desk inside a coworking building. Everything it offers a founder is programme, mentoring, investor introductions and its annual forum. So if you need bench space or equipment, this is not the place to look. How programmes work The shape is the same across AFI's cohorts. A call opens, applications are reviewed, shortlisted founders go through a first round of interviews and then a jury round, and the cohort is announced and onboarded. The two 2026 cohorts each say only 15 to 20 startups are selected. A cohort then runs for about five to six months and ends with a demo day in front of investors and strategic buyers, followed by a valedictory session. Inside a cohort, AFI names four recurring pieces of support. Individual mentoring maps a specialist mentor to the founder's own leadership, sector and business need. Knowledge Building Sessions are monthly expert-led webinars and workshops for the cohort. Learning Community sessions are closed peer groups the startups themselves help run. AFI Huddle is a many-to-one mentor engagement for cross-sector input. Alongside these, cohorts get product refinement, masterclasses, market access, a startup toolkit and investor connects. The agri cohort puts the time commitment at three to four hours a week over five months. Who can apply There is no host-institute restriction here. AFI has no campus and no students of its own, so outside founders apply directly. The Impact Catalyzer sets the tightest bar: an early-stage, tech-driven startup company, a for-profit social enterprise, at technology readiness level 5 or beyond, and operating for more than two years. Having already taken grants, awards or investment is explicitly not a bar to applying. The agri cohort asks for early to growth-stage startups with a working MVP or product, in precision agriculture, automation, agri financing, or dairy and cattle management. The 2026 AI cohorts list a working MVP, initial traction, a strong founding team and a scalable AI use case. None of the pages state an incorporation requirement, a geography gate or a category gate beyond sector. Cost and equity AFI states on its agri cohort page that the programme is free and that it takes no fees and no equity. The other cohort pages do not state a position either way, so ask before you assume. The advisory programme is the exception that is clearly priced: AFI asks founders to write in for pricing, duration and offering details. The annual forum charges a per-person fee for selected startups. Funding and investor access AFI does not run a grant scheme of its own that it publishes. What it offers founders who are actively fundraising is investment-readiness support: a one-to-one pitch deck review and refinement session, a workshop for a selected group covering how to choose the right capital source, IP strategy and valuation, and how to think like an investor, and an investor-matching exercise it calls Investor Dating. Its funding page also introduces 3iPartners, an impact investment fund formed by Silicon Valley entrepreneurs and executives to back agri-tech, health-tech and ed-tech enterprises. Learning, networking and the annual forum The AFI Annual Forum is its flagship event: an invite-only two-day gathering of 100 social innovators and 100 people from impact investment, philanthropy, government, industry and public policy. Eight forums have been held since 2012. The ninth is announced with the theme "Transforming Lives Through Technology and Collaboration" but no date. AFI also runs the Silicon Valley Challenge, an annual business plan competition it says selects five social enterprises from India for a two-week, all-expenses-paid programme in Silicon Valley. Track record AFI's own pages do not agree on how many founders it has worked with: its home page and its get-involved page both say more than 1,000 entrepreneurs have been connected to resources and opportunities, while its fundraising page says it has partnered with more than 100 social entrepreneurs. Neither figure is dated, so we publish neither as a count. What is checkable is the cohort rosters. The Impact Catalyzer's 2024 first cohort lists 23 named startups. Each agri cohort lists 16. AISEA, the accelerator AFI runs with IIT Hyderabad's i-TIC Foundation, is described as having taken 30 social entrepreneurs through two cohorts. Who runs it Sanjay Kadaveru is founder and chairperson. Sam Pitroda is honorary chairman and sits on a board of trustees that also includes Dr. P Vijay Bhatkar, former NASSCOM president Rentala Chandrashekhar, former Rajya Sabha member Rajeev Gowda and Shiv Khemka of SUN Group. A separate board of directors is split between AFI-India and AFI-USA. An AFI Agri Council supplies the agri cohort's mentors, among them Hemendra Mathur of ThinkAg and Emmanuel Murray of Caspian. Locations and careers The New Delhi office is in Mayur Vihar and the Bangalore office is on Brunton Road. The Silicon Valley chapter is in Los Altos, California, there is a US office in Milpitas, and the UK chapter is in London. AFI's careers page lists openings including a chief operating officer, a programme manager, a fundraising manager, a strategic initiatives programme manager and an innovation fellowship.

Name: Afthonia Lab
Description: Afthonia Lab, run by Afthonia Pvt. Ltd., is a fintech and techfin incubator based in Bengaluru. It describes itself as a fintech and techfin incubator that works to turn startups into business-ready ventures over the course of a year. It is based at BTM Layout 1 in Bengaluru, Karnataka. What it is Afthonia Lab presents two kinds of programme, aimed at two different audiences. Its core offering for Indian founders is an incubation programme for fintech and techfin startups. Alongside this, it runs accelerator tracks that are built for overseas scaleups looking to enter the Indian market, rather than for India-based founders. This split is worth noting because the two labels point in different directions. The organisation describes itself on its homepage as a fintech and techfin incubator, while its accelerator work — the Accelerator Program and an accelerator run with Invest NSW — is specifically for scaleups expanding into India. A founder in India looking to be incubated and an overseas scaleup looking to enter the market are both served, but by different programmes. Incubation The Afthonia Incubation Programme is for fintech and techfin startups and runs over about a year. It centres on one-to-one mentorship with fintech experts, industry leaders and subject-matter specialists, and on compliance assistance — regulatory support, compliance and legal advisory aimed at fintech startups. Incubated startups are also offered free credits. The programme positions itself for startups based in India, and selection runs through an application form. India market entry The Accelerator Program is a six-month programme designed to help scaleups expand their businesses in India. It provides strategic guidance, mentorship and networking intended to speed up market entry and business growth. It is aimed primarily at overseas scaleups entering India rather than at India-based founders. A second, related accelerator is run in partnership with Invest NSW, the New South Wales government's investment arm in Australia. This six-month accelerator helps Australian fintech, cybersecurity and green-finance startups expand into India with guidance and market-entry support. It is open to Australian startups in those fields, not to India-based founders. Scale On its homepage Afthonia Lab reports having incubated more than 20 startups. These are the organisation's own figures. Locations Afthonia Lab operates from BTM Layout 1 in Bengaluru, Karnataka. How to apply Applications are made programme by programme. The incubation programme takes applications through an application form linked from its page. The India market-entry accelerators are reached through the listings linked from the Global Programs page; the Invest NSW accelerator is delivered in partnership with Invest NSW rather than through a separate form.

Name: Amazon India
Description: Amazon India backs Indian startups through a corporate venture fund, two accelerator programmes and two seller-onboarding programmes. The fund is the Amazon Smbhav Venture Fund (ASVF), which Amazon launched in 2021 as an India-dedicated fund for early-stage startups. Amazon Global Selling runs the Propel Global Business Accelerator, earlier called the Propel Startup Accelerator, for D2C brands that want to sell abroad, and Amazon Saheli runs Saheli Accelerate with Invest India for women entrepreneurs. Amazon Smbhav Venture Fund ASVF describes itself as an India-dedicated venture fund for early-stage startups and high-quality entrepreneurs. It was announced at Smbhav 2021, Amazon's flagship event for small and medium businesses, and Amazon has since said the fund has been expanded. The fund's own website lists three focus areas: small business digitisation, healthcare and agritech. Amazon's later announcements say the fund began with agriculture and healthcare and has since widened to D2C brands, fintech, gaming and, most recently, consumer-goods manufacturing, with part of the fund set aside for startups that digitise manufacturing in India. The two descriptions differ in emphasis, so check with the fund which areas it is actively backing. The fund says it offers more than capital. Portfolio companies get a dedicated portfolio-development manager to help them work with Amazon teams, PR and marketing opportunities, opportunities to join closed betas of Amazon products, and mentorship from Amazon product leaders. Amazon names several of its portfolio companies, among them The Good Glamm Group, FreshToHome, XYXX, Hopscotch, Fitterfly, Cashify, Acko Insurance, smallcase and M1xchange. ASVF has also signed a memorandum of understanding with DPIIT on the government's priority of making India a global manufacturing hub. This is a partnership, not a recognition held by the fund. Propel Global Business Accelerator Propel is run by Amazon Global Selling, not by the venture fund. It is for D2C brands in consumer goods, from groceries and beauty to bedding, kitchen, apparel and luggage, that want to grow in global markets. Participants get free one-to-one account management, workshops, mentorship from Amazon leaders and venture capital partners, peer sessions and a Demo Day where they pitch to investors. The top three winners share an equity-free grant from Amazon. Amazon Smbhav Venture Fund is named as one of the investor partners. Applicants need to own a consumer-goods brand with a working product and revenue already in place, an applied trademark status in India, a scalable supply chain and a distinct product proposition. Amazon says it looks at India unit metrics, supply-chain scalability, the founding team, the product proposition, the completeness of the application and global-market unit metrics. Season 5 selected 50 D2C brands from more than 500 applicants. Season 4 received more than 900 applications from over 15 cities and selected 54 finalists. Amazon says Propel has supported over 120 Indian D2C brands in four years, including Minimalist, Sirona, Shumee, PLIX, Butterfly Edu and Confect. The programme page shows registrations for the 2025-26 edition as closed, and no later season is listed. Saheli Accelerate Saheli Accelerate is for women entrepreneurs who are ready to scale their businesses. Amazon Saheli launched it in 2025 with Invest India. The first season received more than 400 applications from women entrepreneurs in 14 cities and selected 18. Amazon reports that 10 of the 18 businesses achieved sustained month-on-month growth on Amazon.in. Amazon announced Saheli Accelerate 2.0 at Smbhav 2025. It is planned to support 50 women entrepreneurs in 2026, with a three-day in-person bootcamp and a focus on founders from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. In January 2026 Amazon said it was preparing to launch the second season. Amazon's own pages do not yet give an application link or eligibility rules for it. Seller programmes: Saheli and Launchpad Two other Amazon programmes help businesses start selling on Amazon.in. They are seller-onboarding schemes, not funding or accelerators. The Amazon Saheli seller programme is for women entrepreneurs who want to become Amazon.in sellers. Benefits include a reduced referral fee, onboarding training, account management support at launch, imaging and cataloguing help, and visibility on the Saheli storefront. Applicants must be women entrepreneurs and need proprietorship details, contact details, a bank account, a PAN and a GST registration. NGOs and government bodies that support women entrepreneurs can apply as collaborators. Amazon Launchpad is for startups and emerging brands with a market-ready, consumer-facing physical product that can ship now or within 30 days. It offers launch support, marketing and visibility, branded content tools, insights and brand protection. Amazon's page says it is primarily considering startups funded or supported by its collaborators, crowdfunding platforms, venture capital firms and accelerators, and also says it welcomes applications from all entrepreneurs and emerging brand owners with a unique product. Who can apply The right route depends on what you are building. The venture fund is for early-stage technology startups and does not publish an application form or criteria. Propel is for D2C consumer brands that already earn revenue. Saheli Accelerate is for women entrepreneurs. The seller programmes are for businesses that will sell physical products on Amazon.in. Scale The numbers above are Amazon's own, taken from its announcements and programme pages. They cover individual programmes, so they should not be added together, and Amazon does not publish a single count of startups supported across all of them. Who runs it These programmes belong to Amazon in India. The venture fund has its own website and contact inbox, Propel sits with Amazon Global Selling, and Saheli is an Amazon India initiative. In October 2024 Amazon India also announced a partnership with Startup India under DPIIT to help startups grow through e-commerce, including the Saheli programme for women-led businesses.

Participants get free one-to-one account management, workshops, mentorship from Amazon leaders and venture capital partners, peer sessions and a Demo Day where they pitch to investors. The top three winners share an equity-free grant from Amazon. Amazon Smbhav Venture Fund is named as one of the investor partners. Applicants need to own a consumer-goods brand with a working product and revenue already in place, an applied trademark status in India, a scalable supply chain and a distinct product proposition. Amazon says it looks at India unit metrics, supply-chain scalability, the founding team, the product proposition, the completeness of the application and global-market unit metrics. Season 5 selected 50 D2C brands from more than 500 applicants. Season 4 received more than 900 applications from over 15 cities and selected 54 finalists. Amazon says Propel has supported over 120 Indian D2C brands in four years, including Minimalist, Sirona, Shumee, PLIX, Butterfly Edu and Confect. The programme page shows registrations for the 2025-26 edition as closed, and no later season is listed. Saheli Accelerate Saheli Accelerate is for women entrepreneurs who are ready to scale their businesses. Amazon Saheli launched it in 2025 with Invest India. The first season received more than 400 applications from women entrepreneurs in 14 cities and selected 18. Amazon reports that 10 of the 18 businesses achieved sustained month-on-month growth on Amazon.in. Amazon announced Saheli Accelerate 2.0 at Smbhav 2025. It is planned to support 50 women entrepreneurs in 2026, with a three-day in-person bootcamp and a focus on founders from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. In January 2026 Amazon said it was preparing to launch the second season. Amazon's own pages do not yet give an application link or eligibility rules for it. Seller programmes: Saheli and Launchpad Two other Amazon programmes help businesses start selling on Amazon.in. They are seller-onboarding schemes, not funding or accelerators. The Amazon Saheli seller programme is for women entrepreneurs who want to become Amazon.in sellers. Benefits include a reduced referral fee, onboarding training, account management support at launch, imaging and cataloguing help, and visibility on the Saheli storefront. Applicants must be women entrepreneurs and need proprietorship details, contact details, a bank account, a PAN and a GST registration. NGOs and government bodies that support women entrepreneurs can apply as collaborators. Amazon Launchpad is for startups and emerging brands with a market-ready, consumer-facing physical product that can ship now or within 30 days. It offers launch support, marketing and visibility, branded content tools, insights and brand protection. Amazon's page says it is primarily considering startups funded or supported by its collaborators, crowdfunding platforms, venture capital firms and accelerators, and also says it welcomes applications from all entrepreneurs and emerging brand owners with a unique product. Who can apply The right route depends on what you are building. The venture fund is for early-stage technology startups and does not publish an application form or criteria. Propel is for D2C consumer brands that already earn revenue. Saheli Accelerate is for women entrepreneurs. The seller programmes are for businesses that will sell physical products on Amazon.in. They cover individual programmes, so they should not be added together, and Amazon does not publish a single count of startups supported across all of them. Name: AmpliNxt
Description: AmpliNxt Foundation is a Section 8 (not-for-profit) innovation platform focused on the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operations (AECO) ecosystem. It was established under the aegis of SoftTech Engineers Limited and works from Baner in Pune, Maharashtra. Rather than a single incubator, AmpliNxt runs a set of programmes for founders building for the built environment: cohort accelerators that take startups from a working prototype towards market readiness, a year-round incubation service, and a student hackathon. Its programmes are run for a pan-India audience, and a physical presence in Pune is not required to take part. What they support AmpliNxt's programmes are for startups working in the AECO sector and adjacent fields, including green construction, deep tech, and the use of AI in construction technology. The accelerator cohorts expect a startup to already have a working prototype or a live proof of concept and at least two active team members, and to be solving a clear problem in the built environment. The year-round incubation service is open to startups at pre-product, MVP, or product-with-go-to-market stage that build on technologies such as deep learning, BIM and GIS. The student hackathon is separate: it is open to undergraduate students of any discipline, in teams of one to five, with no prior startup experience and no DPIIT registration required. Programmes AmpliNxt's main offering is NIRMANA-100, a 100-day cohort programme for incorporated AECO startups that is non-equity and runs virtually across India. Its second cohort has applications open. The foundation also runs NEXACON 100, a curated 100-day, non-equity cohort for AECO startups preparing for real industry deployment, which ends in a graduation showcase rather than direct funding. Alongside these it offers a year-round incubation service and the Construct.AI BHARAT hackathon, a student competition built around live infrastructure and city-systems problems such as roads, buildings, traffic, waste and energy. Who runs it AmpliNxt Foundation is a Section 8 not-for-profit, established under the aegis of SoftTech Engineers Limited. It operates from SoftTech Towers on Baner Road in Pune. How to apply Each programme has its own application form on the AmpliNxt Foundation site, where applicants submit company and founder details, their stage of development and a pitch deck. Applications to the incubation service are accepted throughout the year, while the cohort programmes and the hackathon open and close on dated timelines, so the current status is best checked on each programme's page. The site publishes two different general enquiry addresses — info@amplinxt.com in its page footers and info@amplinxtfoundation.com in the body of its contact page — so founders may see either when getting in touch.

Name: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham
Description: Amrita TBI is the Amrita Technology Business Incubator, a non-profit startup incubator run with Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham and supported by the Government of India. It funds, mentors and nurtures ideas, startups and entrepreneurs, and it is based on the Amritapuri campus in Kollam, Kerala. How the programmes work Amrita TBI offers incubation for startups at the idea and growth stages in various sectors, including technology, healthcare and agriculture. Incubation can be physical, with workspace in Kollam and Bengaluru, or virtual, for startups that can operate from anywhere in India. Once accepted, a startup can stay in the programme for up to three years. Its accelerator is a six month programme for information technology (software) startups, from the idea stage through the first few customers. It aims to make each startup ready for investment by the Demo Day. The accelerator page says Amrita TBI does not take equity from startups for joining. The stated application deadline for the accelerator has passed, and the apply page shows applications as closed. Amrita TBI also runs grant and residency routes that come from national schemes. NIDHI-PRAYAS gives a grant to an aspiring innovator or startup to build an idea into a prototype. NIDHI-EIR gives a monthly subsistence grant to an aspiring or budding entrepreneur with a technology business idea. Under the MeitY Startup Hub GENESIS scheme, Amrita TBI runs an Entrepreneur-in-Residence grant and a matching investment programme, which matches investment that an eligible startup raises from venture capitalists and angel investors. Amrita TBI is also a partner incubator for the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, which the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade runs. Its slots are shown as filled. Its PitchFest is a pitch competition for startups, and its last dated deadline has passed. Several of these calls are closed by their stated deadlines. Check the apply page for what is open before you plan an application. Who can apply Incubation: startups in various sectors, including technology, healthcare and agriculture, at the idea and growth stages. Accelerator: information technology (software) startups, from the idea stage through the first few customers. NIDHI-PRAYAS: aspiring innovators and startups that want to build an idea into a prototype. NIDHI-EIR: aspiring or budding entrepreneurs with a technology business idea. GENESIS matching investment: eligible startups. The pages read do not list the criteria. Facilities The Amrita TBI Fab Lab offers prototyping and testing with 3D printing, PCB printing, CNC machines and IoT kits. Incubatees also get workstations with high speed network, meeting rooms and printers. They can use the labs at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, which the site describes as more than 100 multidisciplinary labs. Support and partners Incubatees get mentorship from national mentors and from mentors in Silicon Valley and Singapore. Amrita TBI links startups to VCs and angel investors, and to an intern pool from Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham. Partner discounts of up to 20 percent cover accounting and legal services. The site also lists cloud credits from AWS and a GST exemption for three years for revenue under a set annual limit. Recognition The site says Amrita TBI is one of the approved NIDHI-EIR centres of the National Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board. It also says Amrita TBI is one of the select implementing agencies of MeitY Startup Hub, and a partner incubator for DPIIT's seed fund. It reports a national award for the best startup incubator in 2017. No approval periods are given for these recognitions. Scale The site's pages give different cumulative counts of startups incubated, so no single figure is quoted here. The impact counter on the home page lists 80 key mentors and 145 patents filed. Locations The Kollam office is on the Amritapuri campus at Clappana. Bengaluru is at Amrita School of Engineering, Kasavanahalli. The home page also lists Coimbatore, at Ettimadai, as an incubation location. The incubation page lists only Kollam and Bengaluru.

Name: AspireLabs
Description: AspireLabs is a sustainability-focused accelerator, incubator and co-working space at B-37, Sector 1, Noida, in Gautam Buddh Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh. It backs startups working on waste management, the circular economy and clean technology, and it runs its programmes with industry and development-sector partners rather than on its own. It was founded by Ranjit Singh, who was Global COO and a board member at Polyplex Corporation Limited and before that Managing Director at Kalpataru Power Transmission Limited. What AspireLabs runs Four programmes are described on its site, and they are not all at the same stage of life. FINILOOP Plastic Lab is a 14-month incubation and mentorship programme for early-stage, technology-driven startups in plastic waste management, aimed at helping Jaipur become a plastic-waste-free city. It is supported by the IKEA Foundation and run with WASTE in the Netherlands and Trust of People in India, and it sits inside a wider city-level waste model called FINILOOP, short for Financial Inclusion and Improved Livelihoods Out of Plastics. CleanEdge was a four-month clean-technology accelerator in Delhi-NCR, run with Shriram Institute for Industrial Research and its technology business incubator, and with Polyplex. It ran from February to May 2019 and is closed. EcoVision is a newer two-phase programme for sustainability and circular-economy startups: a first phase of incubation and validation, then a second phase of one-to-one acceleration. Its page names a focus on women and underserved founders. Reimagine Plastic is an open innovation challenge on post-consumer multi-layer plastic packaging, with three named tracks covering collection, turning recycled granules into products, and recovering purer material at scale. Whether you can apply right now You cannot, on the evidence of its own pages. Both programmes with published question-and-answer pages state that applications are closed, the EcoVision page carries an "Apply Now" control that is not wired to anything, and Reimagine Plastic publishes no dates, eligibility or entry route at all. The one thing you can book today is a desk. If you want to be told when a cohort opens, write to the address on the contact page and ask. Who can apply when a cohort is open FINILOOP Plastic Lab wants startups working in plastic waste management anywhere in India, provided they have set up operations in Jaipur and contribute to making the city plastic-waste free. You do not have to relocate to Noida for it. CleanEdge asked for startups in clean technology, broadly read: circular economy, waste management, recycling and up-cycling, plastic and rubber, clean water and clean air, renewables, 3D printing, smart city solutions and environment sustainability. It wanted either a working minimum viable product, or an early-stage company with some customer traction, validation and revenue, and it asked that the business have a direct or indirect impact across social, financial and environmental measures. Applicants could be based anywhere in India. How selection worked CleanEdge published the fullest account. Applications were reviewed within twenty days. Shortlisted teams were invited to a telephone conversation with the review team, with feedback promised to those who did not progress. Survivors presented in person or by video to a selection committee, after which selected teams were offered a term sheet, then went through basic due diligence before joining. FINILOOP Plastic Lab uses two rounds of evaluation and judges startups on problem-solution fit, potential environmental and social impact, team, and business viability. Facilities and co-working AspireLabs sells desks in Noida on monthly plans, with a two-day free trial, a discount for women founders and a month free on a twelve-month booking. The space has brainstorming rooms, phone booths and breakout areas, and the plan includes high-speed internet, lockers, parking, printing, whiteboards, tea and coffee, biometric attendance, a telephone booth, a library and community meetups. Meeting and event space for up to twenty-five or up to forty-five people can be booked in half-day weekend slots with projection and conferencing equipment. During CleanEdge, participants also had access to lab, prototyping, plastic processing and specialty chemicals facilities at Shriram Institute's incubator in North Delhi; that access belonged to that programme, not to AspireLabs. Who runs it Ranjit Singh is the founder. Abhinav Ramaria heads programmes and operations, covering acceleration and incubation, life cycle assessment studies, plastic recycling policy research and deal evaluation. The team also includes an incubation programme associate, an admin lead for the co-working space and an accounts executive. Twelve mentors are named on the EcoVision page. Getting there The office is at B-37, Block B, Sector 1, Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201301, a short distance from Delhi. The site offers a "Schedule a visit" booking if you want to see the space before committing.

FINILOOP Plastic Lab uses two rounds of evaluation and judges startups on problem-solution fit, potential environmental and social impact, team, and business viability. Facilities and co-working AspireLabs sells desks in Noida on monthly plans, with a two-day free trial, a discount for women founders and a month free on a twelve-month booking. Name: AssisTech Foundation (ATF)
Description: AssisTech Foundation (ATF) is a non-profit based in Bengaluru that runs India's first accelerator dedicated to assistive technology. Founded in October 2018, it works with start-ups that build products, devices, software or services for persons with disabilities — it is a programme for founders building assistive technology, not a programme reserved for founders who themselves have disabilities. What they support ATF's programmes are open to start-ups building assistive technology (AT) — devices, software or services that help people with disabilities in areas such as learning, mobility, communication and independent living. Its own materials describe portfolio companies working across a wide range of disability types, including visual, speech and hearing, and physical and intellectual disability. Detailed eligibility criteria are not published; what ATF does describe is validating applicants' products with people with disabilities as "super-users" during the programme, rather than screening founders for their own disability status. Programmes ATF's flagship is the ATF Enabled Acceleration Program, a 16-week cohort for AT start-ups. Selected companies are each assigned an industry-leader mentor and work through growth and investment strategy, product design and management, and an operating plan with milestones, alongside workshops with industry and disability experts and weekly governance and review meetings. The programme ends with a Demo Day in front of industry leaders, investors, government officials and disability experts, and graduates join an active alumni network with regular meetups. Cohorts are put together in batches of 8 to 10 start-ups, following a screening process and jury evaluation. At least one recent cohort ran under the name cATalyst AT Startup Acceleration Program, delivered with SBI Foundation. ATF also runs the ATF Awards, an annual recognition programme that does not charge a fee to enter. Start-ups nominate themselves in Emerging or Established categories, covering innovation, market impact, people's choice and women-led ventures, while NGOs, government bodies, CSR programmes, education institutions and AT investors can be nominated in separate "Enabler" categories. Nominations are screened for completeness and eligibility, evaluators shortlist three entries per category, and a jury makes the final selection before an awards ceremony. A separate ATF Fellowship — a 12-month programme for young professionals with a bachelor's degree or two or more years of work experience, aimed at people who want to work on disability and accessibility issues rather than at founders — has not published a new intake in some time and its stated application deadline has long passed. Support and services Start-ups on the Acceleration Program get access to disability-focused NGOs, associations and beneficiaries, and to government partnerships in the disability space. ATF connects founders with early-stage investors, impact investors, venture capital and corporate social responsibility programmes, and runs webinars, investor pitch sessions and an annual Assistive Technology Conclave. It also offers legal and accounting support and a start-up kit of subsidised software tools and services, plus ongoing alumni mentoring after the cohort ends. Track record ATF's most recently updated pages describe a portfolio of more than 65 start-ups across seven cohorts, offering more than 120 assistive technology products and holding more than 60 patents between them, supported by a network of more than 500 AT start-ups and more than 55 mentors. It reports impacting the lives of more than 1 million people with disabilities. Older pages on the same site give smaller numbers for the same measures — for instance 42 portfolio start-ups across five cohorts — so these figures should be read as a moving count that not every page has caught up with, rather than a single fixed total. ATF also co-founded a global alliance with assistive-technology organisations in several countries, reporting a combined network of more than 1,200 AT start-ups internationally. Who runs it ATF is led by co-founder and CEO Prateek Madhav, supported by a board that includes Paralympian Dr. Deepa Malik, T-Hub CEO Ravi Narayan, and other business and technology leaders. Its accelerator work began with the Karnataka state government's backing, together with Samarthanam Trust, from 2018. ATF also lists open roles on its own careers page, mostly based in Bengaluru. How to apply ATF's dedicated apply page has not carried a working application link for some time, and specific programme calls — including cohort intakes for the Acceleration Program — have historically opened through their own forms rather than a single standing portal. Founders interested in a cohort or the ATF Awards should check ATF's current programme pages directly for open application windows, and can reach the team at its general enquiries address for questions.

Description: AURONE describes itself as an incubator and accelerator for early-stage conscious startups. Applying Both acceleration programmes link to one application form on the website. The application page is titled as the first cohort of conscious startups and founders. The site does not say when the next intake opens or whether applications are open now.

Name: Bangalore Bioinnovation Centre
Description: Bangalore Bioinnovation Centre (BBC) is a life-sciences incubator run as a Government of Karnataka undertaking, inside Helix Biotech Park on the IBAB campus in Electronic City Phase 1, Bengaluru. It works with startups across five sectors: health tech, agri tech, food tech, climate tech and Industry 5.0. How programmes work Founders move through three staged tracks. Pre-Incubate is for early-stage innovators and students who have a promising idea but need to test it — BBC assesses the idea's technical feasibility and market potential, connects them with mentors from academia and industry, and gives access to common instruments and basic lab facilities for early experiments. Incubate is for startups ready to build their product: they get a private, fully furnished wet lab with its own gas, water and power, plus access to central instruments such as mass spectrometry, SEM and flow cytometry without having to buy the equipment themselves, along with co-working space. Accelerate is for growth-stage startups with a market-ready product, and focuses on business scaling — strategic introductions to hospitals, pharma companies and agri-industries for pilots and sales, guidance on regulatory pathways like FDA, CE and CDSCO for going global, and preparing founders for Series A/B fundraising through valuation workshops and investor introductions. BBC's own pages do not state a fixed duration, published eligibility checklist, cost, or equity terms for any of the three tracks, and the site's application page is a simple call-to-action with no listed steps or documents — a founder currently has to apply through the online form or reach the centre by email or phone to learn the specifics. Alongside the three tracks, BBC runs two paid services open to non-incubated organisations too. Co-Manufacturing is a cGMP-compliant common manufacturing facility for taking biologics, enzymes and other bio-products from pilot to commercial scale, with stainless-steel and single-use bioreactors for microbial and mammalian cell culture, filtration and purification systems, and automated filling and packaging lines. Contract Research offers assay design and validation for drug discovery and diagnostics, advanced characterisation using HPLC and LC-MS, and antimicrobial and sterility testing, for external companies, startups and academic institutions that want to outsource R&D rather than build their own lab. Who can apply Each track targets a different stage: Pre-Incubate for early ideas and students, Incubate for startups ready to build a product, and Accelerate for startups that already have a market-ready product. Sector focus spans health tech (bio-electronics, diagnostics, healthcare robotics), agri tech (farm-level innovation, food-business support for FPOs, agricultural engineering including drones and IoT), food tech (processing technology, nutraceuticals, sustainable packaging), climate tech (carbon capture and ESG, bio-energy, circular economy, renewable energy) and Industry 5.0 (human-centric manufacturing, sustainable industry, resilient supply chains). Facilities BBC's Central Instrumentation Facility gives incubated startups shared access to equipment they would otherwise have to buy: a BD FACLyric flow cytometer (12-colour, 3 lasers), bioreactors from BioJenix and Nilsan Nishotech, an SP Virtis Genesis floor-model freeze drier, RT-PCR, a Leica Stellaris confocal microscope, an analytical ultracentrifuge, an LC-MS 2000, an Akta Avant 25 FPLC protein purification system, a Leica Thunder fluorescence imager (DAPI, GFP, RFP channels), and a Waters Xevo TQ-S Micro UPLC-MS system. Incubate-track startups get their own private, modular wet lab with gas, water and power laid on. Separately, the Co-Manufacturing facility adds cGMP-grade bioreactors and downstream processing equipment for scaling up production once a product is ready to manufacture. A general co-working area with meeting and conference rooms rounds out the physical space. As of this research, BBC's dedicated facilities page was still under construction and several programme pages did not yet show real capacity figures. Scale BBC's own cohort page names String Bio, Yostra, Indoor Biotech, Aindra, Terra Blue, Pandorum, Atrimed and VNIR among its incubated startups, and says it has supported "100+ more" beyond those named. Two of its startups have had recent, large funding rounds reported on BBC's own news page: Pandorum Technologies, a regenerative-medicine company, raised a Series B round, and 4baseCare, a precision-oncology company, also raised a Series B round. BBC's pages do not give an overall count of startups supported, survival rate, jobs created or total capital raised across its portfolio. BBC also connects founders to third-party grant schemes rather than running its own grant fund: the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, DST NIDHI's Seed Support System, and K-Tech's Idea2PoC grant-in-aid, plus a BIRAC BioNest grant that funded its own MedTech facility. Its agri-tech work is backed by NABARD and the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana. Who runs it BBC is chaired by Dr. Manjula N, IAS, who is also Secretary to the Karnataka government's Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T. Rahul Sharanappa Sankanur, IAS, Managing Director of the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), sits on the board as a director, alongside Prof. D. Sundar of IBAB, who also holds the Biocon Chair. Dr. Mohamed Adil A.A. is BBC's Managing Director. BBC currently lists no open job positions on its careers page. It runs a regular calendar of workshops and bootcamps, including a recurring Medicos Innovation Bootcamp series for healthcare-innovation students and founders, hands-on IoT and 3D-printing workshops, and a month-long horticulture entrepreneurship programme run with Syngenta Foundation India and the University of Horticultural Sciences. Locations BBC is at Helix Biotech Park, IBAB Campus, Electronic City Phase 1, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560100.

Name: Bharat Inclusion Initiative
Description: Bharat Inclusion Initiative (BII) is a support programme run by IIMA Ventures, a startup incubator established by IIM Ahmedabad. It backs technology startups that want to reach lower-income customers in India. The programme is based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, at IIM Ahmedabad's New Campus in Vastrapur, but founders do not have to move to the city to take part. What it supports BII's current focus is financial inclusion, jobs and livelihood, and skilling. The programme is looking for scalable innovations that can serve lower-income segments such as nano-entrepreneurs, low-income and gig workers, women and migrants. Startups need customers or beneficiaries from lower-income segments, at least in part. Solutions at the prototype, MVP and early-traction stages are preferred, and the programme also says it supports startups from idea to post-MVP stages. You do not need to be a registered company to apply. You do need to be an entity registered in India before selection can be confirmed. How the support works Support is bespoke. IIMA Ventures agrees a set of milestones with each startup, and the startup works toward them with the programme's help. Training, mentoring, technical assistance and market access are provided as needed. Financial support is paid in tranches against the milestones and the funds required, under a service agreement. Recipients may have to provide a utilisation certificate before a later tranche. Regular check-ins run for up to a year. The programme also organises corporate connects and investor demo days, and it helps with one-to-one investor conversations case by case. Startups get showcase opportunities at corporate meetups, demo days and partner events, along with cloud credits and offers from essential service partners. Equity BII takes equity. Startups are onboarded as incubatees, and a mentoring equity of 3-5% is expected. The programme says it will try to provide extra funding through grants or convertible debt via its other programmes, but selection does not guarantee it. Office Hours Founders can also book Office Hours, one-to-one mentoring sessions with mentors from the IIMA Ventures core team and its expert network. Mentors are chosen by theme. Past sessions covered digital lending, payments, ERP, agri-finance, personal finance, GST services and team building. Earlier editions A previous edition of the initiative describes activities that the current programme does not list: a Financial Inclusion Lab that ran six cohorts over 4 years, a Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund that reported 8 investments, and a Bharat Inclusion Champions programme for idea-stage individuals and teams. It also reports 16 Sprints held across 9 cities for more than 400 participants. Those counts are undated and describe earlier work, so check with the programme before assuming any of these is open. Who runs it IIMA Ventures describes itself as a startup incubator established by IIM Ahmedabad. The current programme names the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation as its supporters. The previous edition named a longer list that also included J.P. Morgan, MetLife Foundation and Omidyar Network, so the supporter list is not settled.

Name: Bharatia
Description: Bharatia is the execution platform of the Samarth Bharat Foundation, a non-profit entity established under Section 8 of the Companies Act of India and set up as a company limited by guarantee. It is headquartered in New Delhi, and its stated purpose is to tackle large development challenges by taking proven technologies and scaling them for wider impact. Its best-documented activity is the Environment & Technology Verification (ETV) programme. A note on names worth checking before you apply: the foundation's own homepage and about page describe Samarth Bharat Foundation as the legal representation of Bharatia, while the ETV programme pages state that the ETV programme is managed by Bharatia under the aegis of Samarth Ganga Foundation. The pages name two different foundations, so confirm which entity you are dealing with when you make contact. What they support Bharatia works with technology and solution companies whose product is already proven elsewhere in the world but has not yet been implemented at scale in India or other emerging markets. The ETV programme is described as a technology commercialisation and acceleration programme rather than an R&D programme, so it is aimed at companies that already have a working, proven solution and need a route into the Indian market. Companies are expected to be open to establishing a presence in India, including manufacturing or assembling locally. Beyond the ETV programme, Bharatia describes an organisational mandate of launching First-of-a-Kind (FOAK) commercial-scale demonstration projects and then scaling them, and it announces lists of grand challenges, including a 2025-26 list of climate grand challenges, inviting solutions for mass deployment. These are described as organisational workstreams rather than open-intake programmes with published eligibility, so a founder's clearest route in is the ETV programme. Programmes The ETV programme introduces proven solutions to market and is entered by invitation, with candidates able to submit an Expression of Interest for consideration by an evaluation panel. It has three application categories: Core, for solutions already proven globally but not yet implemented at scale in India or other emerging markets, that are high-impact and whose companies are open to manufacturing or assembling and to establishing a presence in India; Development, for companies at the same solution maturity as Core but without a commercialisation team or strategy yet in place; and Market Access, for companies that do not qualify for Core or Development, or that are already present in India but want ETV validation for market visibility. The programme uses a proprietary methodology it calls VIPERS, with technology, commercial and investment readiness scoring, to structure how each solution is taken to market. Track record Bharatia reports that, as of March 2024, over 60 technologies from 18 countries had gone through the ETV programme. This is the organisation's own figure. How to apply Entry to the ETV programme is by invitation only. Interested companies can submit an Expression of Interest for the relevant category — Core, Development or Market Access — for the evaluation panel to consider, or take part in an ETV introduction workshop. The foundation's contact page offers topic-specific routes to get in touch, including ones to submit a grand challenge or a FOAK or impact project, rather than a single published application form.

Name: Bosch DNA accelerator
Description: Bosch DNA Nxt is the startup alliance programme run by Bosch in India. DNA stands for Discover, Nurture and Align: the programme sets out to discover startups working in Bosch's areas of interest, nurture the engagement, and align the startups with Bosch's business units so the two sides can build something together. It is run by Bosch Global Software Technologies, formerly Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions, a wholly owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH. What it supports The programme sources startups in areas Bosch cares about across mobility, Industry 4.0 and energy, with healthcare and semiconductors named as areas it is opening up. The technologies it looks for include artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, human-machine interaction and AR/VR, sustainability and robotics. The common thread is a solution a startup can take into a Bosch business, rather than a fixed stage or sector filter. How the programme works DNA Nxt is built around co-creation: selected startups work with Bosch business units to build proofs of concept, and the engagement can lead to joint go-to-market work or Bosch investing in the startup. Bosch describes the current intake as a continuous, year-round process, while past editions ran as fixed cohorts. The stated length of an edition is not consistent across Bosch's own announcements, which have described it as both a 12-week and a 16-week programme, so treat the duration as approximate. The sixth edition was run in collaboration with Startup India, the central government's startup initiative, which offered mentoring and the chance for startups to work closely with Bosch business units. Track record Bosch states that the programme has hosted six cohorts since it began, with more than 90 startups graduating, and that it has drawn more than 6,000 applications to take part. It points to outcomes including co-creations and product development, joint go-to-market efforts and investments into startups. These are Bosch's own figures. How to apply The current programme page does not publish an open application form or an intake deadline, and an earlier dedicated website for the programme no longer works. The route Bosch gives is to email the programme team at bgswdnastartup.allianceprogram@in.bosch.com for information or queries. In the past, applications were invited during specific editions. Who runs it The programme is run by Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), the arm of Bosch that was formerly Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions, and which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH.

Description: BrahmVeda, registered as BrahmVeda Ventures Private Limited, is a venture development organisation run by a team of AI practitioners and entrepreneurs, describing its purpose as igniting the fusion of AI brilliance and entrepreneurial passion. It works exclusively with AI-powered ventures, aiming to empower the next generation of AI-driven startups to transform industries and reshape the world. Founders are taken through a structured 4D Framework covering Discover, Design, Develop and Deliver, which carries a venture from an initial concept through to market launch. Alongside that methodology the studio offers hands-on product development expertise, growth strategy support, access to a funding network and an integrated ecosystem of partners. It is led by three co-founders, Nachiket Patel, Vipul Kapoor and Kashyap Pandya, covering AI, growth and strategy respectively. Founders engage by bringing an AI venture idea into the studio's build process rather than through a fixed-date cohort.
