Name: FundEnable
Description: FundEnable describes itself as a full-stack fundraising ecosystem for startup founders. It runs an accelerator, puts its own capital into startups and runs institutional fundraising rounds through its investor network. The company says it has spent the last eight years helping founders turn ideas into fundable businesses. How the programmes work The FundEnable 3 Phase Accelerator is an AI-enabled, three-phase capital-raising accelerator. It combines fundraising education, founder consulting and curated investor access. Its One-to-One Demo Day works through the company's investor network: weeks before the event, FundEnable circulates investment decks, gathers investor interest, learns what each investor is looking for and curates meetings between founders and investors. The company says deals close at its Demo Days. That is its own claim. The accelerator page lists IIM Bangalore's NSRCEL among its marquee incubator partners, and i-Hub, Government of Gujarat among its marquee government partners. Who can apply The accelerator is aimed at founders who are raising capital. Its page does not state entry criteria. FundEnable also lists a three-month experiential internship, the VC Ecosystem Immersion Fellowship. It is designed for students and young professionals who want to understand how venture capital and the startup ecosystem work. It is an internship, not a programme for founders. Capital-raise service Beyond its programmes, FundEnable runs capital raises as an embedded team rather than as a one-time advisory engagement. The company says the work covers strategy, investor outreach and term negotiation, and continues until the round is closed. It also says it has built hundreds of pitch decks and negotiated hundreds of term sheets, some for deals that did not close. Investments The company says it deploys its own capital into high-potential startups and works with them on later fundraising rounds. The site does not describe a way for founders to apply for this investment. Rounds it has advised on The homepage lists several funding rounds it advised on. These include WorkIndia's rounds from Aavishkaar and Beenext, and from Beenext and Xiaomi; EMotorad's round from Green Frontier Capital; Malaki's strategic fundraise from a family office; Luxora's seed round from strategic individuals, including family offices; Task Tracker's seed round from strategic angels and incubator partners; and Iom Bioworks' seed round from Inflection Point Ventures. It also lists a recently closed strategic stake sale for Chikitsa Diagnostic and Ultrasound Training Centre. These are the company's own listings. Scale The company's site counters show more than 3,000 founders trained, more than 200 accelerators run, more than 500 demo days, more than 100 incubators and more than 100 investors and family offices, more than 500 angel investors trained, and more than 10 seed investments. These are self-reported figures. A 2023 third-party report gave a lower count of entrepreneurs at the time, 1,500 or more, so the figures are not settled. Who runs it Its founder and CEO is Dr Vikrant Potnis, according to the company's about page.

The company says the work covers strategy, investor outreach and term negotiation, and continues until the round is closed. Description: GHV Accelerator is the public name of GreenHouse Ventures Private Limited, which runs programmes to connect Indian startups with the Japanese market. Its current, active work on its own site is the India–Japan Startup Gateway (IJSG), a programme that takes selected Indian startups to Japan to meet enterprises, institutions, investors and other ecosystem partners. What they support The India–Japan Startup Gateway is open to India-based startups that want to engage with the Japanese ecosystem, whether for market entry, pilots, business-to-business collaboration or investor access. The programme describes an interest in startups across areas such as AI and machine learning, deep tech, manufacturing, climate and sustainability, robotics, IoT, enterprise SaaS, mobility, semiconductors and electronics, energy, industrial automation, and drones and aerospace. GHV presents itself as an accelerator rather than a campus incubator, and the India–Japan Startup Gateway is the one programme its site currently describes. Programmes The India–Japan Startup Gateway is a market-entry and partnership-building programme. Selected startups travel to Japan for structured interactions with enterprises, institutions, investors and other stakeholders, alongside industry visits. GHV describes it as a paid programme that participants contribute towards, with the contribution covering travel, visa support, accommodation in Japan, the enterprise and ecosystem interactions, industry visits and local logistics. Selection is described as based on sector relevance, business maturity and readiness to engage with the Japanese ecosystem. How to apply Founders apply through the application form linked from the India–Japan Startup Gateway page. The form asks for venture details, year of incorporation, stage, revenue and funding status, and a case for the startup's interest in the Japanese market. Applications are reviewed, and shortlisted ventures may be invited for a follow-up discussion. The programme team can be reached at ijsg@ghvaccelerator.com. A note on its history How long GHV has operated is unclear from the available sources, which do not agree. Its own homepage describes experience spanning more than two decades, while the record this page replaces listed a founding year of 2014; third-party databases also carry the 2014 date. Because the organisation's own pages and these other sources conflict, no single founding year is stated here, and this is worth a human check before publishing.

Name: GSF India
Description: GSF is an early-stage investor in Indian technology startups, founded in 2012. It writes the first cheque to founders at the pre-seed and seed stage, often leads the round, and says it works on a founders-for-founders basis. Alongside its direct investing it runs three programmes: an online consumer cohort for founders, an online course in angel investing, and an angel fund that individual investors can join. Its website does not publish a registered office address. What they support GSF invests at the pre-seed and seed rounds, usually as the first cheque in a startup, and says it can follow on in later rounds. It backs founders who are solving a real problem, typically between the MVP and product-market fit stages, and it welcomes solo founders. It is sector-agnostic. Its pages list investments across Enterprise and SaaS, consumer tech, B2B commerce, generative AI, fintech, deeptech, D2C brands, edtech, healthtech, agritech and robotics. Good Soul Fellas Capital, its angel fund, does not focus on D2C. Programmes GSF Takeoff is an eight-week, zero-equity cohort for pre-product-market-fit founders building consumer businesses. It is run online, with two mentoring sessions on weekdays each week, mentors who are operator-founders, VCs and CXOs, and peer learning in small pods. The programme covers user research, MVP building, distribution, unit economics and fundraising, and it ends with an online demo day and a closed offline demo day in February 2027. Participation carries a fee and there is no equity stake. GSF SuperAngels Academy is an online course in angel investing for working professionals. Its page describes masterclasses from angel investors, live startup pitches and case studies, and sessions on term sheets, valuation, round construction and exits. Participants can invest alongside GSF in early-stage startups. The course charges a non-refundable fee. Its page describes a ten-week programme, and the dates it gives refer to an earlier intake. Good Soul Fellas Capital is a rolling angel fund scheme. GSF sources and diligences the deals and invests in 10 to 12 early-stage technology startups over 12 to 18 months. Investors are invited to monthly screening calls, get one-to-one time with GSF partners, and receive a pass to the annual Founders-Investors Retreat in Goa. The fund is routed through a SEBI-regulated Category I angel fund. Facilities and support GSF's support is mentoring, introductions and events rather than physical space. Takeoff participants get one-on-one guidance with the leadership team, a coordinator for the programme, mock pitch sessions before demo day, and support at both demo days. GSF also runs a founders and investors retreat each year in Goa, a conference in Bangalore (July 2024, held at Shangri-La), and spring mixers. Its network includes more than 200 founders, industry experts and seasoned mentors. Scale GSF reports 110+ companies invested in, on its homepage, and describes the same figure as 110+ investments on its thesis page. Its pages give different counts elsewhere: one partner's biography says 135+ investments in tech startups in India, and the Good Soul Fellas page says over 140 investments. The founder network is 200+ on the homepage and over 300 on the angel fund page. Read these as orders of magnitude, not audited totals. Its portfolio page lists 100 companies, with status labels that include active, acquired and exited. Named companies include Whatfix, MediBuddy, Pratilipi and Drivio. Who runs it Rajesh Sawhney founded GSF in 2012 and is its Founder and General Partner. Nirmal Shah is a Partner, and two analysts source and evaluate deals. The team page describes Rajesh as a serial entrepreneur who has made 135+ investments in tech startups in India, a count that differs from the homepage figure above. Locations GSF Takeoff and SuperAngels Academy are online. The Founders-Investors Retreat is held in Goa; its 2025 edition on 26 June 2025 gathered 150+ participants, including 100 investors and 50+ founders. Its July 2024 conference was held in Bangalore at Shangri-La. The site gives no office address. How to apply Founders can apply to GSF Takeoff through the application form on its programme page, or ask about direct investment through the form on the Get Funding page or by writing to the team inbox. Individuals who want to learn angel investing can register for the SuperAngels Academy through its form. Investors who want to join the angel fund apply through its page for an initial call with the team.

Name: GoMassive
Description: GoMassive Earth Network is a climate-focused organisation based in Gurugram, Haryana, that works with startups solving for climate across sectors. It describes itself as a climate innovation network specialising in open innovation, and it runs its programmes in partnership with Massive Earth Foundation. Its founder, Shailesh Vickram Singh, is also listed as Founder and Director of Massive Earth Foundation. The site does not settle on a single label for what GoMassive is. Different pages present it as a climate innovation network, as an accelerator operator, as a corporate incubator and co-working provider, and as an angel investment network focused on climate. Read together, these describe an organisation that accelerates climate startups, connects them to corporates and investors, and invests alongside a syndicate of funds, rather than a single fixed type of body. What they support GoMassive works with startups building climate and sustainability solutions. Its agri-tech accelerator looks for startups in agriculture and allied sectors, registered as Indian startups with Startup India, that are revenue-positive with at least one paying customer and a technology-led, scalable product. Across its wider work it positions itself around climate technology and digital sustainable solutions. Programmes AgroXLerate, the GoMassive agri-tech accelerator, is a ten-week programme that supports a small cohort of climate-resilient agri-tech startups and ends in a demo day. It is co-hosted by Massive Earth Foundation, G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (Pantnagar), Climate Angels and GoMassive Earth Network. Selected startups receive complimentary cloud and software credits from Google Cloud, Microsoft and HubSpot, along with field-testing access through G.B. Pant University. The programme runs in intakes rather than continuously, and its most recent cycle has closed. GoMassive has also run climate-tech accelerators in partnership with Massive Earth Foundation and larger organisations, including a GoMassive Climate Accelerator cohort run in association with AWS India. These earlier cohorts are shown as closed on the site. How programmes work The agri-tech accelerator is applied to through an online application form linked from the programme page. The provider states that its accelerator programmes are equity-free and charge no fee, with investment considered only on a case-by-case basis through Climate Angels. Because programmes run as intakes, founders should check the programme page for the next open call. Facilities and connections GoMassive does not run its own incubation or co-working space. It states that it has partnered with co-working providers so that startups can choose a partner space and add support such as mentor, investor and industry connects on top. For agri-tech startups, it brokers field-testing access through G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology in Uttarakhand. Track record GoMassive reports that it has supported more than 400 startups with industry connects, mentorship and access to investment, drawing on a panel of more than 50 mentors and a syndicate of over 20 funds. Its pages give different counts for the number of investments it has made directly, so that figure is best checked against the provider. These are the organisation's own published figures. Where they are GoMassive operates from Sector-43, Golf Course Road, Gurugram, Haryana, and lists its open roles in Gurugram. Founders looking for careers, events or partnership information will find dedicated pages on the site.

Name: Hindsight Ventures
Description: Hindsight Ventures is an Africa-focused accelerator and innovation consultancy. It is the Africa subsidiary of Startup Réseau, which its site describes as an India-headquartered global accelerator. It runs bootcamps, challenges and cohort-based accelerators for startups from idea stage to growth stage, mostly in African countries. How its programmes work Most of its programmes are short. Its bootcamps and challenges last from a few days to four weeks, and most run online or in a hybrid format. The JICA NINJA Acceleration Program is a three-month accelerator for growth-stage startups in Uganda. The Growth Acceleration Program in Uganda is hybrid, with about 30% of its components in Kampala and 70% online. The two Wazo Challenge editions are described as validating and mentoring early-stage tech entrepreneurs. The Founder Development Bootcamp is pitched as a route to mentorship, industry access and capital. Its fintech and insurance programmes name a sector focus on their own pages. Some challenges offer a grant to the cohort, and several programmes offer technology credits from partner companies. Check each programme page for what applies to you. Who can apply Most of its programmes name African countries, and most say applicants must be based there. Wazo Challenge Nigeria takes Nigerian nationals aged 18 to 35 who live in Nigeria. Wazo Challenge Tanzania needs a registered entity in Tanzania or Africa. Britam Betalab needs one in Tanzania, Uganda or Rwanda. The AFRISE Challenge takes African youth aged 18 to 35 from eight named countries. The Innovation Managers course is for individuals, and the site names no nationality or country limit for it. Startups outside the named countries should read each programme's eligibility section before they apply. Current intakes Two programmes are marked opening soon, with no dates: the Founder Development Bootcamp and the East Africa FinTech Bootcamp. For the Founder Development Bootcamp, the site names Africa in one place and Tanzania in another, so its eligibility is not yet clear. The Innovation Managers course closed its 2026 applications on 31 July 2026. Its pages give 8 weeks in one place and 12 weeks in another for that course's length. The 2026 application forms for AFRISE and BIOMIC now read that they are no longer accepting responses, so neither can be applied to now. The Africa Innovation Challenge page shows an application link with no date. A founder who wants to hear of a new round should watch the programmes page, since the site gives no standing intake for most of its programmes. The Wazo Challenge Nigeria 2023 edition, the Growth Acceleration Program 2025, the JICA NINJA cohort, the Wazo Challenge Tanzania 2025 and Britam Betalab 2025 are all past. Track record as reported The site reports graduate counts for several programmes, such as the Women LDP, the Absa ReadyToWork platform and the AFRISE Challenge. These figures are self-reported, they count different things for different programmes, and they do not add up to one total. The home page says the organisation has made grants to ten companies across four editions since April 2021. It also claims that its portfolio startups have raised more funding after their programmes. That claim is self-reported. The site does not publish a single count of startups supported. Who runs it and when it began Hindsight Ventures is the Africa-focused subsidiary of Startup Réseau. The site says the organisation began in 2020. Third-party directories give 2012 and 2021 instead. Those listings are unconfirmed, so 2020 is the organisation's own statement. The home page mentions seed and early-stage financing for startups. It does not say whether the organisation takes equity from programme participants. Locations Programmes name Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria, as well as other African countries. The Founder Development Bootcamp and the Africa Innovation Challenge do not name a single country. The site does not publish a postal address for the organisation.

Name: IIHMR Startups
Description: IIHMR Startups is a healthcare accelerator in Jaipur, Rajasthan. It describes itself as a Section 8 registered non-profit organisation and a unit of the IIHMR Foundation, working under the aegis of IIHMR University. It supports health innovators and early-stage startups across healthcare and allied sectors, and says it works at the intersection of healthcare, technology, public health and management. The focus is narrow on purpose. IIHMR Startups lists eight healthcare domains it supports: hospital and care delivery solutions, medical devices and diagnostics, public health, healthtech and digital health, AI and data, clinical research and trials, wellness and preventive care, and healthcare financing. A founder building outside healthcare is not the audience here. How programmes work There is one standing programme, Saamarthya, and a set of events and competitions that run in editions. Saamarthya is a six-month acceleration programme for startups that already have a working product at technology readiness level 4 or above. It runs virtually, in cohorts of ten to fifteen startups, with a two-day residential bootcamp at IIHMR University in Jaipur on go-to-market, sales and growth. Selected startups get hospital pilots and real-world validation access, mentorship from operators, investors and clinicians, regulatory and business guidance, business development introductions, co-working at the Jaipur centre, and a cohort finale in the form of an investor demo day. It charges a programme fee and takes no equity. It also gives each startup a structured support wallet, which IIHMR Startups is explicit is not cash to spend freely: it is deployed against pilots, compliance, legal and financial setup, and technology or infrastructure needs. The other formats are shorter. HealthXchange is a healthcare ecosystem meetup that brings hospitals, market-ready healthtech startups, investors and government representatives into one room, aimed at turning solutions into pilot conversations. The Grand Health Innovation Challenge is an innovation competition for young innovators and early-stage entrepreneurs; its fourth edition drew thirty-seven innovators. CureCode is a thirty-six-hour hackathon where corporates supply the problem statements and startups, students and developers build prototypes against them. The Entrepreneurship Development Bootcamp is a short student programme that colleges can ask IIHMR Startups to run on their own campus. Utkarsh is a healthcare conclave with an investor demo day and an expo. Healthathon was a pitching competition offering grant and seed support to early-stage healthcare startups and innovators. At the time this page was checked, every one of those, including Saamarthya, showed applications or registrations closed. That is normal for a provider that works in editions rather than rolling intakes, but it means the practical route in between cohorts is the contact form, which carries a query type for founders who want to incubate at IIHMR Startups. Who can apply Saamarthya is open to outside founders, not only to IIHMR students or alumni. Its stated bar is a working product tested beyond prototype, post-proof-of-concept or early revenue traction, a healthcare, pharma, medtech or wellness focus, and a formally registered entity, which can be a Private Limited company, an LLP or a Partnership. An unregistered team or a solo founder with an idea does not meet it. The idea-stage routes are the competitions and the student bootcamp. The Grand Health Innovation Challenge takes young innovators and early-stage entrepreneurs. CureCode takes technology-driven startups, students, developers and tech professionals working in AI and machine learning, blockchain, the internet of things, data analytics and digital health. The Entrepreneurship Development Bootcamp is for students and early-stage innovators. Healthathon accepted startups and innovators with an idea, proof of concept, MVP or early revenue, preferably as registered entities. Separately, IIHMR University alumni are invited to engage as mentors, entrepreneurs, enablers or investors through an alumni programme, which offers podcast and speaking slots and an annual alumni award. Facilities IIHMR Startups lists co-working and infrastructure at its Jaipur centre as part of what Saamarthya gives you, alongside access to the research and academic ecosystem around it. It does not publish seat counts, floor area, or any laboratory or testing equipment of its own, so a founder who needs bench or lab space should ask before assuming it is there. What it does describe in detail is access rather than kit: hospital and public health pilot environments, clinicians and domain experts, and regulatory and clinical validation support. Scale IIHMR Startups reports supporting more than eighty startups, with more than twenty at revenue and 576 jobs created. It puts its mentor and expert pool above one hundred and its partner count above fifty, and says it has oriented more than four thousand students. These are its own undated figures rather than audited ones, and its pages do not agree with each other on some of them, so they are best read as an order of magnitude. Its named portfolio includes Aignosis, SocioDent, Medyseva, MedTel Healthcare, NeuraSim, Femease, PregAmie, Kode Blue, Mobilab, Nema AI, Immunyfit, ONCO Connect, Verdant, BLISCare, Bio Hubb, Telidox, Easy Heals, Edith Healthcare, CaresAtHome, Anucool Autism, Jamitson, Living Needs, Nirvesh Enterprises, Mozek, Newbees, Logos Transformation, Ved Sanjeevani, Always Live Yoga and Vini Brawn. IIHMR alumni ventures it names include BootWay and Muditam Ayurveda. It has signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Health Mission, Rajasthan to enable pilot implementations for healthcare solutions, and was onboarded by BHASHINI, a Digital India initiative, as an Anusandhan Mitra. It does not claim recognition as a technology business incubator or an Atal Incubation Centre, and does not state any DPIIT, NIDHI, DST, AIM or MSME status of its own. Who runs it The team named on the site is small: Abhishek Gupta heads investments and corporate partnerships, Kushal Pareek is senior manager for incubation, and Shivam Verma handles marketing and operations. Its board is drawn from IIHMR and outside it, including S.D. Gupta, president of IIHMR, P.R. Sodani, president of IIHMR University, Ayan Agarwal of Transcorp International and Yamini Agarwal of the IIHMR Foundation. R.A. Mashelkar, the former head of CSIR, is listed as chief patron, alongside an advisory board with people from Sun Pharmaceuticals, GSK, Fibe India and Apex Hospitals. Locations There is one location: 1 Prabhu Dayal Marg, Sanganer Airport, Jaipur 302029, on the IIHMR University campus. The phone line is staffed Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 IST, and the team says it replies to email within a day. IIHMR Startups also runs a jobs board advertising roles at startups in its ecosystem, and publishes news, newsletters and a podcast.

Name: IIIT Bangalore
Description: The IIIT Bangalore Innovation Centre (IIITB IC) is the incubation and acceleration arm of International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore, based at Electronic City in Bengaluru. It is a Section 25 company, and the centre says it has worked with entrepreneurs since its inception in 2009. Its stated mission is to build an ecosystem that helps innovators build deeptech solutions for India. How programmes work The centre runs several kinds of programme. Orbit is an incubation programme for deeptech startups that takes a venture from proof of concept to market. ATOM is a twelve-week pre-incubation track for early-stage founders, with versions for health and wellness and for fintech. Its acceleration programmes run for six months and cover healthcare, sustainability and manufacturing, and it also runs a five-day founder bootcamp. Most of these programmes list application deadlines that have already passed, so check each page for an open intake before you apply. Incubatees usually give the centre convertible debentures that convert into a 2 to 5% stake in the company. The centre's policy says the exact percentage depends on the level of involvement and the facilities the company uses, and it is agreed before a company is accepted. Who can apply Incubation is open to a private limited company. A founder who is an employee of a government organisation, or of another outside body, needs a No Objection Certificate from that employer. A company may be incubated only once. Applications for incubation are made online through the centre's portal, and the centre does not have to give a reason if it rejects one. Facilities The centre offers plug-and-play office space and virtual incubation. Its co-working space has closed private seats and open collaborative seating, plus meeting and presentation rooms. Seats are priced per seat per month. Scale The centre's homepage counts 112 startups supported and 87 key mentors. The parent institute's homepage says 50+ startups incubated. The two figures are not reconciled on either site, so read them as rough orders of magnitude rather than audited totals. Credentials The centre describes itself as a MeitY TIDE 2.0 G2 Centre, approved by the Ministry of Electronics and IT as part of MeitY Startup Hub, and as a Government of Karnataka approved incubation facility. Who runs it The centre's team includes Amandeep Srivastava, Chief Innovation Officer and Executive VP of COMET Foundation; Natarajan S, Mentor-in-Residence; Manugowda M S, Program Manager; Swathy V, Incubation Manager; and Lakshmikanth B N, Incubation Associate. Partners The centre works with Wadhwani Foundation (Liftoff sessions), the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (strategic knowledge partner for ATOM FinTech), BPL Medical Technologies (FLASH), the Bangalore Chamber of Industry and Commerce (Smart Manufacturing), NIMHANS (DEEPAS clinical mentors), and MeitY under the TIDE 2.0 scheme. Life in the incubator Incubatees must send the centre information about material changes, such as a change of name, business, directors or shareholders, new equity or debt, or a new bank facility. They submit quarterly reports, which the centre uses to track milestones. Incubation normally runs for the agreed period, and the centre can grant up to two extensions of six months each. The policy also lists when a company must leave: when the incubation period ends without an extension, when the business is not viable, when it raises substantial outside investment, or when its annual revenue or profit passes the policy's thresholds. Locations The centre's address is 26/C, Hosur Road, Electronics City Phase 1, Electronic City, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560100.

Name: IIM CALCUTTA INNOVATION PARK
Description: IIM Calcutta Innovation Park (IIMCIP) is a Section 8, not-for-profit company set up in 2014 under the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta. It is recognised as a Technology Business Incubator by the Department of Science and Technology, and it is based on the IIM Calcutta campus at Joka, Kolkata. What they support IIMCIP organises its work into four stages: Immersion (hackathons and seminars that introduce students and aspiring founders to entrepreneurship), Pre-Incubation (helping early-stage innovators take an idea to a prototype), Incubation (helping startups reach product-market fit) and Acceleration (helping startups already generating revenue scale further). Across its programmes it works with founders in social impact, sustainability and the circular economy, agri-tech, fintech, edtech, healthcare and deep tech, as well as mobility and manufacturing through its programme with Maruti Suzuki. A number of its programmes are aimed specifically at underserved regions and rural livelihoods, including women-led enterprises linked to self-help groups. Programmes IIMCIP's incubation offer gives resident startups furnished office space on the IIM Calcutta campus, along with a virtual incubation option for founders who cannot be based in Kolkata. Two seed-funding schemes, NIDHI Seed Support and the DST-NSTEDB Seed Support Program, are open to startups that have spent at least three months in either incubation track, are registered in India with Indian promoters holding at least 51% shareholding, and use the funds for product development, testing, market entry or related costs. On the acceleration side, the Kotak BizLabs Accelerator Programme is a CSR initiative of Kotak Mahindra Bank that takes 20 early-revenue-stage startups working on social or environmental impact through mentorship, capacity-building bootcamps, business-model and go-to-market guidance, and investor readiness support, ending in a demo day in front of Kotak leadership and investors. The Bengal Business Accelerator Program is a similar acceleration track focused on West Bengal's micro-enterprises and MSMEs. On the pre-incubation side, Maruti Suzuki NURTURE is a joint programme with Maruti Suzuki for very early-stage startups in eastern, north-eastern and central India working on mobility, manufacturing and social-impact ideas. Shortlisted teams go through regional idea hunts, a grand idea hunt and mentoring, and the strongest teams get a guided visit to a Maruti Suzuki manufacturing facility, access to Maruti Suzuki's ecosystem and alumni network, and a shot at a paid proof-of-concept. The Prakriti Incubation Launchpad, run with the Pernod Ricard India Foundation, is a 12-month programme for early-stage circular-economy and sustainability startups, moving a cohort of ten through mentorship and capacity building down to a final cohort of five for a demo day. IIMCIP also runs the Social Impact Incubation Programme and the long-running TATA Social Enterprise Challenge for social entrepreneurs, and it has recently added new state and sector partnerships, including a Jharkhand Incubator Programme with the Jharkhand State Livelihood Promotion Society for women-led rural enterprises, and a role as technical agency on an IFAD-backed agroecology project. IIMCIP also has a track record in the North East and rural India that goes beyond a single Kolkata campus. It has run the North East Entrepreneurship Development Program with the North Eastern Council across all eight north-eastern states, giving prototype and commercialisation grants to shortlisted entrepreneurs, and it has run a rural incubation programme in Assam for women-owned enterprises linked to self-help groups, in partnership with the Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission Society. Neither of these states a separate branch office; they describe state-wide or region-wide programme delivery rather than a satellite campus. Facilities and support Startups accepted into physical incubation get furnished office space on the IIM Calcutta campus, with internet, printing and conferencing facilities, at no charge. Beyond space, IIMCIP offers mentorship from IIM Calcutta faculty, alumni and outside entrepreneurs and investors; help raising equity or debt funding and introductions to angel and institutional investors; support services such as legal, secretarial, IT, HR and payroll help from partner firms at preferential rates; and structured training programmes on building and scaling a business. Track record IIMCIP says it has helped more than 1,000 startups achieve significant growth. Its partners over the years have included government bodies such as the Department of Science and Technology, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the North Eastern Council, along with corporates such as Tata Sons, HDFC Bank, Balmer Lawrie, IDFC FIRST Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Maruti Suzuki India. Who runs it IIMCIP's governing body includes IIM Calcutta's Director, Alok Kumar Rai, and Deans Bhaskar Chakrabarti and Vivek Rajvanshi, alongside external members such as T.N. Hari, co-founder of Artha School of Entrepreneurship, and Arun Malhotra, former MD of Nissan Motors India. Day-to-day operations are led by Chief Operating Officer Pranjal Konwar, Chief Business Officer Gaurav Kapoor and Chief Finance Officer Debapratim Das, with a team of programme, incubation and communications staff based in Kolkata. IIMCIP's careers page lists current openings, all based in Kolkata. Locations IIMCIP is based at the IIM Calcutta campus, Diamond Harbour Road, P.O. Joka, Kolkata 700104.

Name: IIMA Ventures
Description: IIMA Ventures is the startup incubator of the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIM Ahmedabad). It was known as IIMA-CIIE, and publicly as CIIE.CO, until it rebranded to IIMA Ventures in 2024. CIIE stands for the Centre for Innovation Incubation and Entrepreneurship, the academic centre at IIM Ahmedabad where the work began in 2002. It is based on the IIM Ahmedabad campus in Vastrapur, Ahmedabad, and also incubates, accelerates and invests in startups from offices in other Indian cities. The Department of Science and Technology (DST) recognised it as a Centre of Excellence in 2019. It calls its model a continuum: incubation, acceleration, pre-seed and seed investing, and incubating venture funds, backed by research on entrepreneurship. It started iAccelerator in 2009 and Powerstart, a climate accelerator, in 2011. How programmes work IIMA Ventures runs a changing set of programmes, most of them with a corporate, foundation or government partner. Open or rolling ones include Kotak BizLabs Season 3 (with Kotak Mahindra Bank), Women's Economic Empowerment and the Bharat Inclusion Initiative (both supported by the Gates Foundation), the Aerospace & Defence Acceleration Fund (with Jaivel Aerospace), the Bharat ClimateTech Initiative (with MUFG), the #BuildingForHer programme for women's financial inclusion, and Studio, its venture studio. Some programmes have a fixed deadline, while others review applications on a rolling basis. Its site lists more than twenty past programmes. They include Swanari TechSprint with the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH), North East Growth Lab with SAP, the People and Culture Accelerator, the AI Summer Residency, Kotak BizLabs Seasons 1 and 2, the Assam Agribusiness Growth Lab, the India Innovation Growth Programme, NIDHI EIR, The Power of Ideas and several hackathons. All of these are now closed. IIMA Ventures is also the west-zone lead incubator under MeitY's TIDE 2.0 scheme, and has been a partner incubator for the Ministry of Defence's iDEX programme since 2018. Support differs by programme. Several offer grant support to selected startups. Some of the programmes with more hands-on support take equity: the inclusion and women's programmes ask for a mentoring equity stake when a startup is onboarded as an incubatee. Others, such as Kotak BizLabs, take no equity. The People and Culture Accelerator charges a fee. Incubation and investing Incubation usually lasts about six months and can run from three to twelve months, with extensions. It can be physical or virtual. Office space at the Ahmedabad centre is not free, but it is offered below market rates. You do not need a registered company to apply for incubation, though some funding programmes require one. Decisions take under two weeks for some programmes and up to 45 days for those with wider outreach. Money is usually released within a month of investment committee approval. IIMA Ventures also invests from its own balance sheet at pre-seed and seed. It is sector-agnostic, with three themes: deep tech, digitalisation and climate tech. At pre-seed it looks for founder-market fit, and at seed it also wants to see the product in use. It has incubated venture funds, including Infuse Ventures in 2011, Bharat Innovation Fund and Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund in 2017, and GradCapital in 2021. Who can apply Most programmes are open to founders from across India, not only to IIM Ahmedabad students. IIMA Ventures generally backs early-stage startups. Each programme sets its own rules: Kotak BizLabs needs DPIIT recognition and paying customers, North East Growth Lab took only startups from the North East, and IIMAvericks is for current IIM Ahmedabad students. You can apply to more than one programme, and support from another incubator does not rule you out. Facilities The Ahmedabad centre has over 50,000 sq ft of space on the IIM Ahmedabad campus. Paid Co Circle membership gives access to the centre. The centre does not offer a mailbox, and its address cannot be used to register a company or for GST. Locations IIMA Ventures has offices in Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Indore and Guwahati, though one of its own pages lists only Ahmedabad, Indore and Jaipur. In Jaipur it set up Startup Oasis with RIICO, its first regional incubator, in 2014. In Indore it runs the Indore Smart Seed Incubation Center (ISSIC) with Indore Smart City. In Guwahati it has hosted bootcamps for North East Growth Lab. It also has teams in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Delhi. Scale IIMA Ventures says it has funded over 340 startups: more than 300 from its own balance sheet at pre-seed and seed, and 40 through the funds it has incubated. It reports 35+ profitable exits from its seed portfolio. It says The Power of Ideas evaluated over 16,000 business ideas, and that BII has accelerated 50+ inclusive fintechs. These are its own figures. Startups in its portfolio include Agnikul, Bellatrix Aerospace, Setu, Kaleidofin, Guvi and Unbox Robotics. Who runs it Priyanka Chopra is CEO and Managing Partner. The leadership team also includes co-founder Kunal Upadhyay, who is Managing Partner of Bharat Innovation Fund, and partners for incubation, seed investing and research. The board includes IIM Ahmedabad's director, Bharat Bhasker, IIM Ahmedabad faculty, and Sanjeev Bikhchandani, the founder of Info Edge. The work runs through CIIE Initiatives, the recognised technology business incubator; CIIE Regional Innovation Foundation, for regional incubation; and CIIE Advisors, which manages its funds. Events and careers IIMA Ventures holds events such as bootcamps, demo days, summits and the monthly #BuildingForHer forum. Its careers page lists jobs and internships and a two-year Analyst Program for people who want a career in venture capital. Its portfolio startups post their jobs on a separate page.

Name: IIT Ropar Technology Innovation Foundation
Description: IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation is a Section 8 company that runs iHub – AWaDH, the Agriculture and Water Technology Development Hub, on the campus of the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar in Rupnagar, Punjab. The hub is a Technology Innovation Hub set up under the Department of Science and Technology's National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS). It runs incubation and acceleration programmes for deep-tech startups, and startups from outside the campus can apply. How programmes work The hub does not run one single incubator. It runs a set of separate programmes, each with its own page, intake and rules. Some are always open, some open for a window each year, and some are run with a partner company or a government body and close after one edition. The two entry points that stay open most of the time are the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme and SPRINT. Under the seed fund scheme, the hub is one of the incubators a DPIIT-recognised startup can choose when it applies on the national Startup India portal. SPRINT, short for Strategic Program for Research, Innovation and Next-Gen Tech Commercialization, takes applications on a rolling basis and also runs open innovation challenges. SAMRIDHI is the hub's acceleration programme. It is built around an annual conclave where startups pitch to investors, and its brochure lists ten support steps that include mentoring, legal help, a demo day, help with investor deals and technology development. The hub has also hosted the intake window for MeitY's GENESIS scheme, a challenge for deep-tech startups in smaller cities, and sector programmes with partners in real estate, water and sanitation, and agriculture. Who can apply The hub's focus is agriculture, water and cyber-physical systems. In practice its programme pages also cover climate technology, geospatial and drone startups, electronics and semiconductor design, AI and machine learning, IoT, and real estate and construction technology. The shared eligibility notes on its pages say it looks for innovative technology and deep-tech ideas, that patents and IP are preferred, that women founders are encouraged to apply, and that individuals can apply, not only registered companies. Individual programmes add their own conditions. The seed fund scheme is for startups recognised by DPIIT and incorporated no more than two years before the application. GENESIS lists its focus areas as electronic design and manufacturing, deep-tech software and products, AI and machine learning, IoT, and VLSI and semiconductors. The partner programmes ask founders to solve one of a listed set of problem statements. Applications are not limited to Punjab. The SAMRIDHI brochure reports that the first conclave, in 2023, received responses from 29 states and union territories. How funding works The hub's funding differs by programme, and its pages do not always agree with each other on size, so this page does not quote amounts. The shape is what matters when you choose where to apply. The seed fund scheme gives a milestone-linked grant for proof of concept, prototype work or product trials, and a separate investment route through convertible debentures or debt for market entry and scaling. SPRINT says funding after screening, an internal pitch and a demo day can come as a grant, as equity or as a loan. SAMRIDHI's brochure describes funding as grant or equity. Check the programme page for the form of money on offer before you apply, because a loan and a grant ask very different things of a founder. No page we read states a participation fee for any programme. Past and partner programmes Several programmes have closed. REAL, the Real Estate Acceleration Launchpad, was run with Omaxe Limited for real estate, construction and PropTech startups. Applications closed in June 2025 and its demo day was in September 2025. SWACH, for water and sanitation startups, was run with Innovation Mission Punjab and the India Sanitation Coalition and closed to applications in June 2024. The WATER Innovation Challenge ran in February and March 2024 with HDFC Parivartan and had four water and agriculture problem statements. GENESIS at IIT Ropar closed to applications on 5 November 2025. The site also lists other programmes whose pages carry no dates, so we cannot say whether they are open: 100 Startups 100 Days, a national programme for early-stage deep-tech startups; DTC Accelerate for climate-tech startups, run with NASSCOM; the PRAGATI micro-accelerator for agriculture startups, funded by Puri Oil Mills Limited; and an Entrepreneur-in-Residence programme. The hub also acts as a recognised Geospatial Innovation Accelerator under the Department of Science and Technology's Operation Dronagiri, where selected geospatial startups get mentoring and technical guidance. There is no separate application route for that on its page. Scale These are the hub's own figures and carry no dates. Its about page says it has incubated more than 150 startups, while its home page counts a portfolio of more than 200 startups. We show the lower, incubated figure. The home page also reports more than 820 jobs created. On its seed fund page the hub says it has funded 32 startups under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme. The SAMRIDHI brochure, dated December 2024, lists nine editions of SPRINT. Who runs it The foundation is a Section 8 company, which means it is a not-for-profit company, set up to support the hub at IIT Ropar. The hub is funded by the Department of Science and Technology under NM-ICPS. The site has separate role inboxes for startups, partnerships, skilling and people. It also has a Hiring section, where it posted its Entrepreneur-in-Residence call in August 2025. Location and contact The hub is in the M. Visvesvaraya Block at IIT Ropar, Rupnagar, Punjab 140001. Its contact page and the footer of its pages give different room numbers, so check before you visit. Startups can write to startups@ihub-awadh.in, and the general inbox is contact.awadh@iitrpr.ac.in. The phone number on the contact page is 01881 232601.

Name: ISB I-Venture
Description: I-Venture @ ISB is the entrepreneurship and incubation platform of the Indian School of Business, run out of ISB's Hyderabad and Mohali campuses. It brings together three pillars under one brand: DLabs in Hyderabad, the Atal Incubation Centre (AIC ISB) in Mohali, and I-Venture Immersive (ivi). A one-year anniversary event held in September 2022 puts its launch at around September 2021. Who can apply — and who can't A founder looking at I-Venture @ ISB needs to know which door they're at, because the platform runs two different kinds of programme side by side. ISPROUTE, its pre-incubation programme, is open only to ISB's own postgraduate students — the current edition is restricted to the PGP Class of 2027. The Technology Entrepreneurship Program's Tricity Edition is similarly restricted, but to engineering students at partner colleges in the Mohali-Chandigarh-Panchkula region, reached through campus roadshows rather than a public form. Everything else — I-WIN, LoopX, the Web3X Incubation Program, the Industry 4.0 Incubation Program, the Agri Incubation Program, and the DST-backed Business Incubation Cohort at DLabs — is open to outside founders with no ISB affiliation required. The one common thread on the open programmes is that most ask for a startup already registered as a company in India. Programmes I-WIN (Women in Innovation) is the flagship accelerator: a programme for women founders or co-founders, holding at least a quarter of the equity and an active decision-making role, who already have revenue and are raising between pre-seed and pre-Series A. It runs as a closed cohort, with a strategy and execution gap analysis at the start, expert-led sessions on go-to-market and financial planning, one-to-one mentorship, brand and performance-marketing labs, and a demo day in front of investors. Four cohorts have run so far. LoopX is a circular-economy accelerator built with the venture fund Tavasya Capital, aimed at pre-seed to Series-stage startups converting waste streams into resources; Tavasya is involved from day one rather than joining at a later funding round. The Web3X Incubation Program, run with Crewsphere, backs early-stage startups building on the Internet Computer Protocol, with non-dilutive grants and mentorship, though selected startups give up equity in exchange for the programme's support. The Industry 4.0 Incubation Program, with Rx100 Startups, works with smart-manufacturing startups that already have a basic prototype, and can lead on to Rx100's own equity-linked acceleration track for startups that complete it. The Agri Incubation Program, run with Samunnati, supports agricultural startups, researchers and enterprises with mentorship, market access and legal guidance. DLabs also runs a sector-agnostic Business Incubation Cohort backed by the Department of Science and Technology, offering physical and virtual incubation with a shot at seed funding, and the platform hosts the government's Startup India Seed Fund Scheme as an eligible incubator. I-Venture @ ISB has also run a series of shorter, sector-specific accelerators over time — in clean energy, gaming, healthcare, fintech and blockchain, electric vehicles, edtech, D2C and social impact, several with named corporate partners. As of this review most of these have closed application cycles rather than open ones; a founder interested in a specific sector should check the individual programme page for a current call before assuming it is running. Facilities and support I-Work @ ISB is the platform's co-working offer, with private office suites and dedicated desks at both DLabs in Hyderabad and AIC-ISB in Mohali, plus meeting rooms, event space, and a shared makerspace and UI/UX lab at the Mohali campus. Startups admitted into the Industry 4.0 and Agri programmes get access to further shared infrastructure through ISB — advanced laboratories and smart-manufacturing hubs for hardware teams, and laboratories, greenhouses and farmland for agri teams. Across its programmes, I-Venture @ ISB also offers regulatory and policy guidance, help preparing for investor pitches, and support connecting startups to potential customers and partners. Track record On its own pages, I-WIN reports four cohorts, more than 50 women-led startups supported, and 85% of founders saying they would recommend the programme. Companies that have come through I-Venture @ ISB's various programmes and are listed in its portfolio include Vecmocon Technologies, Cercle X, GreenPod Labs, Satyukt, Qzense Labs, NeuroPixel.AI Labs and BioPrime AgriSolutions, spanning EV components, waste-to-value, agritech and enterprise software. Who runs it Saumya Kumar is Director of I-Venture @ ISB and CEO of DLabs; Naman Singhal is CEO of AIC ISB. The advisory board includes ISB Dean Madan Pillutla, Kalaari Capital managing director Vani Kola, Threshold Ventures partner Heidi Roizen, and Cardekho.com co-founder and president Umang Kumar, alongside government and academic representatives. How to apply There is no single application form for the platform as a whole. Each programme carries its own apply page and its own calendar — I-WIN and LoopX run as periodic cohorts with defined call-for-application windows, while ISPROUTE opens only around the start of each ISB academic year for its own students. General queries can go to I-Venture @ ISB's role inbox rather than a named individual.

Name: India Accelerator
Description: India Accelerator is a multi-stage, fund-led startup accelerator headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana, and run by IA India Accelerator Pvt. Ltd. Its own site describes it as founded in 2018. It works with early-stage and growth-stage founders through a set of accelerator programmes, a venture studio, an investment arm called Finvolve, an angel-matching platform called IAngels, mentoring, and support for startups expanding abroad. What they support India Accelerator names five investment theses it focuses on: Defence and Aerospace; Energy, Mobility & Connectivity; Singularity/GenAI; Impact & Energy; and Healthcare. Elsewhere it describes its portfolio as spanning GenAI, fintech, SaaS, healthtech and deep tech. It works across the founder journey, from early-stage teams through to growth-stage companies preparing for a later funding round or exit. Programmes Its Accelerator Programs sit under one standard structure but are organised into named sector tracks: IA-iAgri for agriculture, IA Cipher for cybersecurity, IA Deep Tech, IA'B2B Tech, IA Finseed for fintech, and IA Pulse. The site does not give each track its own duration, eligibility or intake calendar — they share the same standard offering (below) rather than being run as separate structured programmes. Its Venture Studio takes a different starting point: rather than accepting already-formed startups, it identifies ideas it considers high potential, builds an MVP around them, and launches the result as a company, providing the resources a founder needs to get that far. Finvolve is India Accelerator's investment arm, described as one of the largest B2B networks for startup investment in India. It backs companies from pre-seed through to pre-IPO across three funds: an Accelerator Fund for early-stage startups, a Seed Fund for startups building toward product-market fit, and a Growth Fund for later-stage companies preparing for an IPO or acquisition. The Accelerator and Seed Funds run on a two-year deployment period with a five-year exit window; the Growth Fund runs on a shorter eighteen-month deployment with a three-year exit window. IAngels is a separate platform connecting startups with a global network of angel investors and mentors. Startups build a profile, including a pitch video, and a matching algorithm connects them with investors whose stated preferences and criteria fit. The platform then supports the conversations that follow, including due diligence, and gives founders access to legal and financial professionals for the transaction. IAngels describes itself as sector-agnostic, citing tech, healthcare and consumer goods among the startups it has hosted. For founders looking to expand outside India, India Accelerator runs a Global Expansion programme built around partner accelerators in five other countries: Silicon Valley Accelerator in the United States, iAccel GBI in the UAE, GINSEP in Germany, 01 Booster in Japan, and The Big Leap Accelerator in Australia. It frames this as market access, exposure to international investors and partners, and support navigating local regulation. Facilities and support India Accelerator runs its own coworking brand, IA Spaces; its homepage claims 36 locations, though it does not list them individually. Startups on its accelerator programmes get a standard package that includes legal, accounting, technology and marketing support, office space, mentorship, and platform credits with AWS, Zoho and GCP, on top of access to the Global Accelerator Network and corporate perks from its partners. Mentorship is organised around a mentor board that spans healthcare, mobility and energy, robotics and technology, waste management, and defence and aerospace, alongside analytics and product development expertise. Founders are matched with mentors suited to their stage and specific challenges, and get access to workshops, training sessions and industry events alongside one-on-one guidance. Track record India Accelerator states two different totals for how many startups it has supported: its homepage cites 220+, while its organisation pages and platform pages cite 200+. Read the figure as an order of magnitude rather than a precise count. It describes itself as DPIIT-recognised and a member of the Global Accelerator Network, and says it was named Best Accelerator of India in 2022 in an award from the Government of India. Its portfolio page names 40 companies it has worked with, including Advance Mobility, Clean Motion, IG Drones, Janitri, Lawyered, Matter, Store Hippo, Dozee, Cashe, InCred Finance, Sunfox and HappiMynd. Who runs it The leadership team named on the site is Ashish Bhatia, Founder and CEO; Mona Singh, Co-Founder and Director; Abhay Chawla, Co-Founder and COO; Munish Bhatia, Co-Founder; Deepak Sharma, Co-Founder and Managing Partner; and partners John Thomas and Arindam Mukhopadhyay. How to apply Startups apply through an online form linked from the site's "Apply as a startup" page. The page itself does not lay out the eligibility criteria, required materials or selection steps in any text a visitor can read outside the form.

Name: India Sanitation Coalition
Description: The India Sanitation Coalition (ISC) is a water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) platform hosted at FICCI Federation House in New Delhi. It brings government and the private sector together on sanitation work. For startups, its main offer is the SWACH Accelerator, a programme for early-stage WASH and waste innovators that ran its first cohort in 2024 and 2025. What the SWACH Accelerator is The SWACH Accelerator was conceived by the India Sanitation Coalition at FICCI along with Innovation Mission Punjab and IIT Ropar. It is meant to give private-sector sponsors a dedicated platform to engage with and support entrepreneurs, startups and businesses working on innovation in this sector. The accelerator has three pillars. Innovation Mission Punjab supports early-stage startups, from prototype and beyond, with mentoring and business support to prepare them for commercialisation. IIT Ropar offers technical assistance to help startups scale. ISC acts as the enabler, recognising and validating the work of startups in the WASH sector. Who it is for The accelerator looks for solutions in four areas: water supply management, sanitation access, hygiene enablement and waste management. It covers the whole value chain of build, use, maintain, treat and reuse, and gives preference to climate-resilient startups working in the WASH sector. If you build a product or process for water, toilets, waste handling or hygiene, this is the audience it is written for. Founders in other sectors will not find a fit. How the first cohort worked The programme officially launched in April 2024 and invited applications from startups and entrepreneurs. Outreach events and roadshows were held in Delhi/NCR on May 2 and 3, 2024. Applications were screened, and a jury meeting finalised the selected startups. The first cohort launched in July 2024 with ten startups: Integerspin, Celligo, GreenBrigade, Paving+, InWaste Technologies, Econscious, Aryav Eco-friendly Resources, Nanokriti, New Unnat India Techno Solution and Innovation, and Green Aadhar. The acceleration ran as structured contact sessions. The first, in June 2024, covered business models. The second, in July 2024, covered financial modelling with a social impact view. The third, in August 2024, covered fundraising and the impact investment landscape. A pitch readiness workshop followed in September 2024. Industry mentors from across India joined the sessions. A Demo Day was held on 14 February 2025 at FICCI Federation House in Delhi, where startups presented to investors and stakeholders. Selected startups are to receive continuous mentorship and handholding support for fundraising. What the partners provide Innovation Mission Punjab is a collaboration between the Punjab Government and the private sector. It says it has engaged with over 1,900 startups. IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation, through its AWaDH hub, is the technical partner and provides testing and development facilities, lab access, patent facilitation and support for commercial research. ISC itself provides techno-managerial support, links stakeholders, and helps corporates invest in startups. Awards and events ISC also runs the ISC-FICCI Sanitation Awards, which it says have recognised more than fifty corporate houses since 2017, and the Rashid Kidwai innovation in sanitation awards (RAKIS) for WASH startups, held alongside its annual conclave. The 2021 RAKIS launch offered a fully sponsored two-year incubation prize at SINE-IIT Bombay in two categories: municipal sewage and municipal solid waste. Status and how to reach ISC The pages we read describe the first cohort as complete and do not announce a second open call. Fees and equity terms are not stated. To ask about the next round or to join as a partner, write to the ISC team or use the contact form on its site. ISC is at FICCI Federation House, Tansen Marg, New Delhi 110001.

Name: Indian Institute of Technology Jammu
Description: I3C – IIT Jammu, the Institute Incubation and Innovation Council, is the innovation and entrepreneurship arm of IIT Jammu. It is a section-8 not-for-profit company, incorporated in March 2021, and its office is at NH-44, Jagti, Nagrota, in Jammu and Kashmir. How the council works I3C says it supports the entrepreneurial pursuits of future business leaders in Jammu, Kashmir and beyond. Its site groups support into three stages. Ideate covers brainstorming, market research and concept development for early ideas. Validate covers testing a product or business model in the market, with mentoring and networking. Accelerate covers advanced resources and accelerator programmes for startups that are ready to scale. Programmes Catalyst 30 is an equity-based seed funding programme for early-stage startups that already earn revenue. It is launched by I3C with support from SIDBI, under the SIDBI Seed Equity Support Scheme. The Mentoring Clinic is a single window where entrepreneurs submit a query and are matched with a mentor. Its first 2 hours of mentoring are free. Who can apply Catalyst 30 is open to startups that are registered and recognised by DPIIT and have generated consistent revenue for at least 6 months. It is sector-agnostic. The Mentoring Clinic is open to aspiring entrepreneurs, early-stage founders, student innovators and MSME owners. Portfolio The portfolio page lists current incubatees, among them startups in deep-tech aerospace, robotics, agritech, ESG reporting and heritage conservation. The page does not give a total count, and the counters on the home page show zero, so this page does not publish a total. Who runs it I3C is chaired by the Director of IIT Jammu, Prof. Manoj Singh Gaur, and its director is Dr. MT Arvind.

Name: Indian School of Business
Description: DLabs, the incubation and acceleration arm of the Indian School of Business (ISB), is based on the ISB Hyderabad campus in Gachibowli. It is a not-for-profit Section 8 company set up by ISB in collaboration with the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India. How programmes work DLabs runs a mix of pre-incubation, incubation and accelerator programmes. The current pre-incubation route is ISPROUTE, a 10-week programme for aspiring entrepreneurs moving from an idea towards a proof of concept. The accelerators are themed: ed-tech (EduRISE 2.0), AI, blockchain and DeFi (FinChAIn, with Broadridge India), MVP-stage startups from T1, T2 and T3 cities (Liftoff Propel, with Wadhwani Foundation), fintech for the informal economy (Build for Billions, with the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub), and agri and food (with Deshpande Startups). Who can apply Each programme sets its own audience. ISPROUTE is open to ISB Co '27 students and is sector agnostic. Several accelerators ask for startups that are at least one year from incorporation and have an MVP, a product or early revenue. Check each programme for its own criteria. Facilities DLabs offers a co-working space for startups. Co-working desks and private offices are also available at DLabs in Hyderabad and at AIC-ISB in Mohali. Scale The DLabs site says it has supported over 200 startups. Who runs it DLabs is led by a CEO and a team of programme, partnerships and finance managers. Its governing body includes ISB faculty and a director of BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus. Locations DLabs is on the ISB Hyderabad campus, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, Telangana 500111. Co-working space is also offered at AIC-ISB in Mohali.

Name: Innomax Startup Advisory
Description: Innomax Startup Advisory is a startup consulting and advisory firm. It describes itself as more than a consulting firm, and it sells its support to founders as a set of advisory services rather than as time-bound cohorts with named batches. Its website is innomaxstartup.com, and the firm can be reached at info@innomaxstartup.com. What they support Innomax works with early-stage entrepreneurs who have an idea or a minimum viable product, and with growth-stage startups looking to optimise operations and connect with investors. Its acceleration page states that a fully developed product is not required to apply, and that it accepts early-stage startups with an MVP or a solid business idea. The firm exposes five distinct service lines on its site: mentorship, acceleration, incubation, funding-readiness support, and a coworking space. These are described as ongoing service offerings, so there are no published intake dates or open-or-closed status for any of them. Programmes The acceleration offering is described as typically running for three to six months, with intensive coaching and investor pitching. The incubation offering is described as typically lasting six to twelve months depending on a startup's progress, and is positioned for early-stage founders who need a strong foundation before scaling. Alongside these, Innomax runs a mentorship offering tailored for professionals, startups and companies, and a funding-readiness advisory service that helps startups become investment-ready through pitch and business-plan work and introductions to angel investors, venture capitalists and funding organisations. There is a point to flag on funding. Innomax's incubation page states that the firm does not directly fund startups, and instead connects them to investors, grants and funding institutions. At the same time, several of its pages advertise funding access, funding opportunities and funding support, which can read as the firm providing capital itself. The site is not consistent on this, so treat Innomax as an adviser that brokers investor introductions rather than a source of capital. Facilities and support Innomax provides a startup-friendly coworking space designed for founders, freelancers and growing teams. It describes hot desks, dedicated desks, private offices that are fully equipped for teams needing privacy, and meeting and conference rooms for client and investor meetings, with high-speed internet and round-the-clock access for premium members. The space is described only as being in a business district, with no address published. Across its services, the firm offers mentorship, business-development support such as product validation, market research and legal structuring, and investor-readiness support. How to apply Innomax does not publish an application form, portal or deadline for any of its services. The acceleration and incubation pages describe an application-and-selection step in which applications are reviewed to select startups, and the mentorship service begins with an initial consultation and needs assessment. In practice the only route in is the generic contact form on the site, or email to info@innomaxstartup.com.

Name: Innovation Mission Punjab
Description: Innovation Mission Punjab, also written IMPunjab and named Punjab Innovation Mission in its policy documents and payment forms, is a public-private partnership that runs programmes for startups, student innovators and school students in Punjab. It is headquartered at Kalkat Bhawan in Aerocity, Mohali. It was launched on 1 September 2021 and describes itself as a catalyst organisation established through collaboration between the Government of Punjab and private-sector stakeholders, and as a dedicated and independent body rather than a government department. How the programmes work The mission says it works through three levers: Pollination, meaning mindset and ecosystem building; Acceleration, meaning structured scaling support; and Capital Access, meaning venture funding pathways. Its startup programmes follow roughly that order of maturity. Fail Fast is a two-week, fully virtual programme for founders who want to validate an idea before building. It uses structured frameworks, workshops and mentor office hours, and it runs in numbered cohorts. Its homepage card describes it as a six-week sprint, while the programme page and the live registration form both say two weeks. Decode is a programme for early-stage startups that already have a registered company and one executed pilot. Its application form describes a 12 to 14 week programme with a deck audit, work on the value proposition, one-to-one strategy sessions and pitching to raise pre-seed capital. The Decode programme page frames the same programme as validation of customer needs and product-market fit, so read it as a mix of both. GTFO is a fundraising-readiness programme with rolling intake. It covers investor-ready materials, pitch decks, financial models, investor mapping and warm introductions, with support continuing until a term sheet closes. The core programme runs for about four weeks, followed by investor engagement support. It is not equity based. The IMPunjab Accelerator is a four-month programme for startups with early traction, a strong team and ambitions to grow from Punjab to global markets. It combines mentorship, execution support, partnerships and investor access. The SWACH Accelerator is a separate programme for startups working in water, sanitation, hygiene and waste management. It offers structured mentorship, pilot opportunities and ecosystem support, and it is presented as a joint initiative with collaborating organisations rather than an IMPunjab-only product. Three programmes are for students. The Campus Ambassador Program lets college students in Punjab represent IMPunjab on their campuses and organise startup events. Eureka helps school students turn ideas into ventures through hands-on learning and mentorship. The School Internship Program is a four-week experience for students in Classes 8 to 12. Who can apply Eligibility differs sharply by programme. Fail Fast accepts idea-stage and MVP-stage founders, alone or in teams, and its form asks whether you or your startup is based in Punjab. Decode needs a registered company, at least one executed pilot, some value addition to an existing product, process or business model, and at least one full-time founder, in any sector. The IMPunjab Accelerator requires DPIIT recognition and a presence in Punjab through operations, registration or incubation. Startups with early revenue or at least one commercial pilot are preferred, and it is open to every sector. SWACH is for startups in water, sanitation and waste with a product or prototype ready for market or scaling. Startups that have run at least one commercial pilot are preferred, startups up to five years old are eligible, and women founders are strongly encouraged. GTFO is for startups with a working product, early traction and a clear intent to raise. The student programmes are open to enrolled students: college and university students in Punjab for the Campus Ambassador Program, school students for Eureka, and Classes 8 to 12 for the School Internship Program. Eureka does not require a startup idea or prior experience, and it is designed to fit alongside school hours. Fees and equity Fail Fast and Decode are paid programmes, and both are equity-free. Fail Fast charges a subsidised fee for participants from India and a higher fee for international participants, and prices per startup whether you join alone or with a team. Decode also charges a subsidised programme fee. The Accelerator, and any other programme that involves fundraising, carries a standard success fee. The Campus Ambassador Program is free for selected participants. The pages for Eureka, the School Internship Program, SWACH and the Accelerator do not state a participation fee, so confirm that with the team before you apply. Facilities Decode participants get free co-working space for three weeks, which they can use at any time during the programme. The School Internship Program runs its sessions at the IMPunjab Innovation Space and follows a hybrid format, with offline sessions and periodic online mentor conversations. A Co-Working Space link appears in the site navigation, but no separate page describes it, so do not assume desks are available outside Decode. Scale, as the programme pages report it All figures below are the mission's own and have not been checked independently. Fail Fast reports 11 cohorts completed, 206 startups validated, participants from 10 countries and 7 Fail Fast Fairs. Decode reports 3 cohorts, more than 66 startups supported and 41 percent women-led startups. The Accelerator reports 43 startups, with more than 100 investor partners, more than 100 deep dives and more than 1,200 mentoring hours. Its page names three cohorts of startups, and those lists add up to one more than the counter. For the mentor network, the Accelerator page says more than 180 mentors and experts, while the homepage says more than 200 mentors across product, engineering, go-to-market, legal and fundraising. The Campus Ambassador Program reports over 200 ambassadors, 240 campus events, over 16,500 students engaged, 30 partner colleges and 15 districts covered. Eureka reports 180 students enabled and more than 50 ventures initiated. SWACH reports more than 100 direct jobs created and more than 420 mentoring hours. Who runs it The mission was conceptualised in 2020. A Group of Experts chaired by Montek Singh Ahluwalia recommended a structured innovation mission as a response to entrepreneurial talent leaving the state. Pramod Bhasin, founder of Genpact, Asha Impact and Clix Capital, is Chairman. The board includes senior industry figures and two senior Government of Punjab officials from the Indian Administrative Service. Somveer Anand is CEO and Mission Director, and Ashish Mehta is Chief Operating Officer. Location and contact The office is at Kalkat Bhawan, Block-C, Aerocity, Airport Road, Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar (Mohali), Punjab 140603. The general inbox is info@impunjab.org. Individual programmes publish their own registration pages, and several of the student programmes run public events and campus activities across Punjab.
